description: A box of seven diatomic molecules, each two medium gray atoms joined together
caption: A box of seven identical diatomic molecules, each two medium gray atoms of the same kind joined together, as in O₂ or N₂ gas. Only one kind of atom appears, so the box shows a pure element even though its particles are molecules.

title: Particle diagram of a substitutional alloy (brass)
description: A lattice of light gray copper atoms with some replaced by dark gray zinc atoms of similar size, with a key
caption: A lattice of light gray atoms, labeled copper in the key, in which eight have been replaced by dark gray zinc atoms of about the same size. This is a substitutional alloy like brass: atoms of the second metal take the places of the first.

title: Analog pH meter reading 8.46
description: An analog pH meter whose needle points to 8.46 on a 0 to 14 dial, with a magnified view of the needle
caption: An analog pH meter with a needle over a dial numbered 0 to 14 and marked every 0.2. The needle sits between the 8.4 and 8.6 marks, a little past 8.4, so the reading is 8.46, with the hundredths digit estimated. A magnified view shows the needle against the marks.

title: pH meter reading 3.27
description: A digital pH meter with its electrode in a beaker, the display reading pH 3.27
caption: A digital pH meter wired to a glass pH electrode standing in a beaker of solution. The display reads 3.27, so the solution is acidic. A digital meter is read exactly as shown, to two decimal places.

title: pH paper showing an acid: pH 2
description: A strip of universal indicator paper turned red, above a pH color chart from 0 to 14, matching pH 2
caption: A strip of universal indicator (pH) paper whose wet end has turned red-orange, above a color chart with one swatch for each whole pH from 0 to 14. The strip matches the pH 2 swatch, so the solution is strongly acidic. pH paper is read to the whole number, and the figure needs color printing.

title: pH paper showing a base: pH 11
description: A strip of universal indicator paper turned deep blue, above a pH color chart from 0 to 14, matching pH 11
caption: A strip of universal indicator paper whose wet end has turned deep blue, above the 0 to 14 color chart. It matches the pH 11 swatch, so the solution is basic. Pair it with the acid strip to ask which solution is which.

title: Identify the element from its photoelectron spectrum
description: An unnamed element’s photoelectron spectrum with five peaks and blank lines in place of the sublevel labels
caption: The photoelectron spectrum of an unnamed element, for students to identify: five peaks with blank lines where the sublevel labels go, on a numbered electrons axis so each peak’s height can be read. The peaks hold 2, 2, 6, 2 and 5 electrons from left to right, 17 in all, which is chlorine.

title: PES comparing magnesium and sodium
description: Photoelectron spectra of magnesium, solid, and sodium, dashed and gray behind it, with a key naming each
caption: The photoelectron spectrum of magnesium drawn solid, with sodium’s dashed and gray behind it and a key naming each. Every magnesium peak sits to the left of the matching sodium peak, because magnesium’s extra proton holds each sublevel’s electrons more tightly, and its 3s peak is twice as tall, holding two electrons to sodium’s one.

title: Photoelectron spectrum of calcium on a broken axis, in eV
description: The photoelectron spectrum of calcium drawn as bars on a broken binding energy axis in eV, with six sublevel labels
caption: The photoelectron spectrum of calcium, 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶ 4s², drawn as bars. The binding energy axis, in electronvolts, is broken into a linear stretch for each group of nearby peaks, with break marks between them, so the core and valence peaks can all be read.

title: Photoelectron spectrum of iron
description: The photoelectron spectrum of iron with seven peaks from 1s² to 4s², the 3d⁶ peak just left of the 4s² peak
caption: The photoelectron spectrum of an iron atom, 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶ 3d⁶ 4s², on a broken binding energy axis in MJ/mol, each group of nearby peaks given its own stretch. The 3d peak sits just to the left of the 4s peak: although 4s fills first, its electrons are held less tightly, which is why iron loses its 4s electrons first when it forms ions.

title: PES of neon with binding energies
description: The photoelectron spectrum of neon with three peaks, 1s², 2s² and 2p⁶, each labeled with its binding energy in MJ/mol
caption: The photoelectron spectrum of neon: three peaks, 1s², 2s² and 2p⁶, with each peak’s binding energy in MJ/mol written over it. The 2p peak is three times as tall as the others because it holds six electrons, and the 1s peak is far to the left because those electrons are held most tightly.

title: Photoelectron spectrum (PES) of sodium
description: The photoelectron spectrum of sodium: four peaks labeled 1s², 2s², 2p⁶ and 3s¹, binding energy in MJ/mol decreasing from left to right on a logarithmic axis
caption: The photoelectron spectrum of a sodium atom, as in AP Chemistry: one peak for each sublevel, labeled 1s², 2s², 2p⁶ and 3s¹, each as tall as its number of electrons, so the 2p peak is three times as tall as the 1s. Binding energy in MJ/mol falls from left to right on a logarithmic axis, so the tightly held 1s electrons are at the far left and the single valence 3s electron at the far right.

title: Activation energy with and without an enzyme
description: Energy diagram with no numbers on its axes: a reaction’s path without an enzyme and a lower dashed path with an enzyme, each activation energy marked
caption: A reaction with and without an enzyme, as biology courses draw it: the shape matters, so the potential energy axis has no numbers. With the enzyme, dashed, the transition state is lower, so the activation energy is smaller, while the reactants and products stay where they are. A key names the two paths.

title: Enthalpy level diagram for the Haber process
description: Energy level diagram with N₂ + 3H₂ on a line at 0 kJ and 2NH₃ on a lower line at −92 kJ, with an arrow labeled ΔH = −92 kJ between them
caption: An energy level diagram for the Haber process, N₂ + 3H₂ → 2NH₃: no curve, just the reactants and products as lines, with the ΔH arrow pointing down from the reactants at 0 kJ to the products at −92 kJ. The reaction gives out 92 kJ of heat, so it is exothermic.

title: Potential energy diagram of an endothermic reaction
description: Potential energy diagram of an endothermic reaction: products higher than the reactants, with arrows for Ea, the reverse Ea and ΔH
caption: The potential energy of an endothermic reaction: the reactants at 20 kJ/mol, the transition state at 150 kJ/mol and the products higher than the reactants, at 80 kJ/mol. Arrows mark the forward activation energy from the reactants, the reverse activation energy from the products, and ΔH, pointing up from the reactants to the products.

title: Potential energy diagram of an exothermic reaction
description: Potential energy diagram of an exothermic reaction: reactants at 50 kJ/mol, a transition state at 150 kJ/mol and products at 20 kJ/mol, with arrows labeled Ea = 100 kJ/mol and ΔH = −30 kJ/mol
caption: The potential energy of an exothermic reaction against the reaction coordinate. The curve runs flat at the reactants, 50 kJ/mol, rises to the transition state at 150 kJ/mol and falls to the products at 20 kJ/mol. The activation energy arrow runs up from the reactants to the peak and the ΔH arrow down from the reactants to the products, each labeled with its value, and a dashed line carries the reactants’ energy across to both.

title: Potential energy diagram with and without a catalyst
description: Potential energy diagram of an exothermic reaction with a dashed catalysed path over a lower transition state, the activation energies of both paths marked, and a key
caption: An exothermic reaction with and without a catalyst. The uncatalysed path, solid, rises to a transition state at 150 kJ/mol; the catalysed path, dashed, to one at 100 kJ/mol. Both start at the same reactants and end at the same products, so ΔH is the same, but the catalysed activation energy is 50 kJ/mol lower. A key under the graph names the two paths.

title: Potential energy diagram worksheet: which arrow shows ΔH?
description: Potential energy diagram of an exothermic reaction with three arrows lettered A, B and C for the activation energy, ΔH and the reverse activation energy
caption: An exothermic reaction with its three arrows lettered for a question: A, the activation energy, from the reactants up to the transition state; B, ΔH, from the reactants down to the products; and C, the reverse activation energy, from the products up to the transition state. Students say which arrow shows which energy and read the values from the numbered axis.

title: Two-step reaction energy profile with an intermediate
description: Reaction energy profile of a two-step mechanism: two transition states with an intermediate in the dip between them, each step’s Ea marked, and ΔH
caption: The energy profile of a reaction that happens in two steps. Each step has its own transition state, a peak, at 120 and 100 kJ/mol, with an intermediate in the dip between them at 70 kJ/mol. Each step’s activation energy runs up from the level before it, so the first step, with the larger activation energy, is the rate-determining step. ΔH runs from the reactants to the products.

title: Digital thermometer reading 78.4 °C
description: A digital thermometer with its steel probe in a beaker, the meter reading 78.4 °C
caption: A digital thermometer: a handheld meter wired to a steel probe standing in a beaker of liquid. The display reads 78.4 °C, about the boiling point of ethanol. A digital reading is taken exactly as displayed.

title: Fahrenheit thermometer reading 98.6 °F
description: A liquid-in-glass thermometer in degrees Fahrenheit, marked every 2 °F, reading 98.6 °F
caption: A liquid-in-glass thermometer scaled in degrees Fahrenheit, marked every 2 °F and numbered every 20 °F. The column ends just past the 98 °F mark, read as 98.6 °F, normal body temperature. Each mark is 2 °F, so students must count by twos.

title: Kelvin thermometer reading 295.4 K
description: A liquid-in-glass thermometer in kelvins, reading 295.4 K
caption: A liquid-in-glass thermometer scaled in kelvins, marked every 1 K from 260 to 390 K, with gray liquid. The column ends between 295 and 296 K, read as 295.4 K (22.25 °C). Kelvin is written without a degree sign.

title: Thermometer reading 22.6 °C
description: A liquid-in-glass thermometer with red liquid reading 22.6 °C, with a magnified view of the top of the column
caption: A liquid-in-glass thermometer marked every 1 °C from −10 to 110 °C, its red liquid ending a little past halfway between 22 and 23 °C. The reading is 22.6 °C, with the tenths digit estimated. A magnified view shows the top of the column against the marks.

title: Thermometer reading below zero: −4.5 °C
description: A liquid-in-glass thermometer with blue liquid reading −4.5 °C, below the 0 °C mark
caption: A liquid-in-glass thermometer with blue liquid whose column ends below 0 °C, halfway between −4 and −5 °C. The reading is −4.5 °C. Use it to check that students count down from zero correctly.

title: Strong acid–strong base titration curve
description: Titration curve of 25.0 mL of 0.100 M HCl with 0.100 M NaOH, with the equivalence point at 25 mL and pH 7 marked
caption: The pH of 25.0 mL of 0.100 M hydrochloric acid (HCl) as 0.100 M NaOH is added, up to 50 mL. The pH starts low, stays nearly flat, then jumps sharply through the equivalence point at 25 mL. For a strong acid and strong base, the equivalence point is at pH 7.

title: Strong base–strong acid titration curve
description: Titration curve of 25.0 mL of 0.100 M NaOH with 0.100 M HCl, the pH falling from about 13 to about 1.5, with the equivalence point marked
caption: The pH of 25.0 mL of 0.100 M sodium hydroxide (NaOH) as 0.100 M HCl is added, up to 50 mL. The pH starts high, stays nearly flat, then drops sharply through the equivalence point at 25 mL and pH 7.

title: Titration curve worksheet: find the equivalence point
description: Titration curve of a weak acid with NaOH, with the equivalence and half-equivalence points marked by dots and blank lines for students to label
caption: The titration of 20.0 mL of 0.150 M formic acid (HCOOH, pKa 3.75) with 0.120 M NaOH, graphed to 40 mL. The equivalence and half-equivalence points are marked with dots and dashed lines to the axes, each with a blank line for students to name it. Students can read the equivalence volume and the pKa off the graph.

title: Weak acid–strong base titration curve
description: Titration curve of 25.0 mL of 0.100 M acetic acid with 0.100 M NaOH, with the half-equivalence and equivalence points marked
caption: The pH of 25.0 mL of 0.100 M acetic acid (CH₃COOH, pKa 4.76) as 0.100 M NaOH is added, up to 50 mL. The pH rises slowly through the buffer region, then steeply at the equivalence point, 25 mL, which is above pH 7. The half-equivalence point at 12.5 mL is marked too, where the pH equals the pKa.

title: Weak base–strong acid titration curve
description: Titration curve of 25.0 mL of 0.100 M ammonia with 0.100 M HCl, the pH falling, with the equivalence and half-equivalence points marked
caption: The pH of 25.0 mL of 0.100 M ammonia (NH₃, pKb 4.75) as 0.100 M HCl is added, up to 50 mL. The pH falls, slowly through the buffer region and then steeply at the equivalence point at 25 mL, which is below pH 7. The half-equivalence point at 12.5 mL, where the pH equals 14 − pKb, is marked too.

title: Volume of a cube in cm³, on a scale marked every 2 cm³
description: Two 100 cm³ graduated cylinders marked every 2 cm³: water at 46.0 cm³ before, and at 61.0 cm³ after a cube is added
caption: Two 100 cm³ graduated cylinders, marked every 2 cm³ and numbered every 20 cm³, so students first work out what each mark is worth. Before, the water is at 46.0 cm³; after a cube is dropped in, it is halfway between the 60 and 62 cm³ marks, at 61.0 cm³. The cube’s volume is 15.0 cm³.

title: Volume of 3 marbles by water displacement
description: Two 25 mL graduated cylinders: water at 12.00 mL before, and at 15.50 mL after three marbles are added
caption: Two 25 mL graduated cylinders, marked every 0.5 mL and numbered every 5 mL. Before, the water is at 12.00 mL; after three marbles are dropped in, it is at 15.50 mL. The three marbles together have a volume of 3.50 mL.

title: Volume of a metal cube by water displacement
description: Two 50 mL graduated cylinders with magnified views: water at 20.0 mL before, and at 28.0 mL after a cube is added
caption: Two 50 mL graduated cylinders, each with a magnified view of its meniscus. The water reads 20.0 mL before and 28.0 mL after a cube is dropped in, so the cube’s volume is 8.0 mL (8.0 cm³). Pair it with the cube’s mass for a density question.

title: Volume of a metal cylinder by water displacement
description: Two 10 mL graduated cylinders: water at 5.20 mL before, and at 7.45 mL after a small metal cylinder is added
caption: Two 10 mL graduated cylinders, marked every 0.1 mL. The water reads 5.20 mL before and 7.45 mL after a small metal cylinder is added. The metal cylinder’s volume is 2.25 mL, read to the hundredth of a mL.

title: Volume of a rock by water displacement
description: Two 100 mL graduated cylinders: water at 50.0 mL before, and at 63.5 mL after a rock is added
caption: Two 100 mL graduated cylinders side by side, labeled Before and After. The first holds water at 50.0 mL; in the second a rock rests on the bottom and the water has risen to 63.5 mL. The rock’s volume is the difference, 13.5 mL.

title: 10 mL graduated cylinder reading 7.36 mL
description: A 10 mL graduated cylinder with blue liquid reading 7.36 mL, with a magnified view of the meniscus
caption: A 10 mL graduated cylinder marked every 0.1 mL and numbered every 1 mL, holding blue liquid. The bottom of the meniscus is a little past halfway from the 7.3 to the 7.4 mL mark, read as 7.36 mL with the hundredths digit estimated. A magnified circle shows the marks around the meniscus.

title: 1000 mL graduated cylinder reading 640 mL
description: A 1000 mL graduated cylinder with green liquid filled to 640 mL, marked every 10 mL
caption: A 1 L (1000 mL) graduated cylinder marked every 10 mL and numbered every 100 mL, holding green liquid. The bottom of the meniscus is on the 640 mL mark, so the reading is 640 mL, the ones digit being the estimated one. There is no magnifier, so students read it from the whole cylinder.

title: 25 cm³ graduated cylinder reading 18.25 cm³
description: A 25 cm³ graduated cylinder reading 18.25 cm³, with a dotted line from the bottom of the meniscus to the marks and a magnified view
caption: A 25 cm³ graduated cylinder marked every 0.5 cm³ and numbered every 5 cm³, with the scale printed in cm³ rather than mL. A dotted line runs from the bottom of the meniscus across to the marks, halfway between the 18.0 and 18.5 cm³ marks, so the reading is 18.25 cm³. A magnified circle shows the marks around the meniscus.

title: 250 mL beaker reading 160 mL
description: A 250 mL beaker with red liquid at 160 mL, between its 150 and 175 mL marks
caption: A 250 mL beaker marked every 25 mL and numbered every 50 mL, holding red liquid a little under halfway from the 150 mL mark to the next mark, 175 mL. Beaker marks are coarse, so the volume is estimated to the whole mL: 160 mL. Use it to compare how precisely a beaker and a graduated cylinder measure.

title: Buret reading 12.35 mL
description: A 50 mL buret reading 12.35 mL, with a magnified view of the meniscus between the 12 and 13 mL marks
caption: A 50 mL buret, numbered from 0 at the top down to 50 and marked every 0.1 mL, with a stopcock at the bottom. The bottom of the meniscus is halfway between the 12.3 and 12.4 mL marks, so the reading is 12.35 mL. A buret reads downward, so the numbers grow toward the bottom of the magnified view.

title: Graduated cylinder reading 34.5 mL
description: A 100 mL graduated cylinder filled to 34.5 mL, with a magnified view of the meniscus between the 30 and 40 mL marks
caption: A 100 mL graduated cylinder marked every 1 mL and numbered every 10 mL, holding gray liquid. The bottom of the meniscus sits halfway between the 34 and 35 mL marks, so the reading is 34.5 mL, with the tenths digit estimated. A magnified circle beside the cylinder shows the meniscus against the marks.

title: Meniscus close-up: 50 mL graduated cylinder at 26.0 mL
description: A magnified view of a meniscus in a 50 mL graduated cylinder, its bottom resting on the 26 mL mark
caption: Only the magnified view of a 50 mL graduated cylinder, marked every 1 mL, with the bottom of the meniscus resting exactly on the 26 mL mark. Because the liquid is on a mark, the estimated digit is 0 and the reading is 26.0 mL. Use it to show students where on the curved surface to read.

title: AD–AS graph worksheet: label an inflationary gap
description: Black and white AD–AS graph of price level against real GDP with no numbers on the axes: a vertical line, a downward-sloping line and an upward-sloping line, the last two crossing at a dot to the right of the vertical line, with dashed lines from the dot to both axes; blank lines for students to write on beside each line, the dot, the price level at the axis, the two outputs at the real GDP axis, and under a brace below the axis between the vertical line and the dashed line
caption: A worksheet graph of an inflationary gap in black and white, every label left as a blank line for students. AD and SRAS cross to the right of LRAS, with dashed lines to the price level and real GDP axes, and the gap between that output and full-employment output is braced under the axis. Blank lines wait for the names of the three curves, the equilibrium, the price level, the two outputs and the gap.

title: Long-run self-adjustment from a recessionary gap on the AD–AS graph (SRAS shifts right)
description: AD–AS graph of price level against real GDP with no numbers on the axes: a downward-sloping blue AD line, a vertical green LRAS line, and a red SRAS₁ line crossing AD at a dot labeled E₁, to the left of LRAS; an arrow points right to SRAS₂, which crosses AD lower down on LRAS at a dot labeled E₂. Dashed lines run from E₁ to both axes and from E₂ to the price level axis, marked PL₁ and the lower PL₂ on the price level axis and Y₁ and Yf on the real GDP axis, and a brace under the axis from Y₁ to Yf is labeled Recessionary gap
caption: An economy returning on its own from a recessionary gap to full employment, with aggregate demand unchanged, drawn with no numbers. AD and SRAS₁ cross at E₁, at real GDP Y₁, short of full-employment output Yf where LRAS stands, and the gap is braced under the axis. SRAS shifts right to SRAS₂, which crosses AD on LRAS at E₂: real GDP rises to Yf and the price level falls from PL₁ to PL₂.

title: Negative supply shock on the AD–AS graph: SRAS shifts left (stagflation)
description: AD–AS graph of price level against real GDP with no numbers on the axes: a downward-sloping blue AD line, a vertical green LRAS line, and a red SRAS₁ line crossing AD on LRAS at a dot labeled E₁; two arrows point left to SRAS₂, which crosses AD higher up and to the left of LRAS at a dot labeled E₂. Dashed lines to the axes mark PL₁ and PL₂ on the price level axis and Y₂ and Yf on the real GDP axis, and a brace under the axis from Y₂ to Yf is labeled Recessionary gap
caption: A negative supply shock from long-run equilibrium, drawn with no numbers. AD, SRAS₁ and LRAS meet at E₁, at full-employment output Yf. SRAS shifts left to SRAS₂, which crosses AD at E₂: the price level rises from PL₁ to PL₂ while real GDP falls to Y₂, as in stagflation. The recessionary gap from Y₂ to Yf is braced under the axis.

title: Numbered AD–AS graph from a schedule: equilibrium at price level 90 and real GDP 8,800
description: AD–AS graph on numbered axes with gridlines, price level from 60 to 140 by 10 and real GDP from 6,000 to 10,500, numbered every 1,000: a blue AD line falling through a dot at each row of the schedule, from 6,400 at a price level of 130 to 10,000 at 70; a red AS curve rising through its dots from 6,500 at 70, steepening to 9,900 at 130; and a vertical green line at 9,500 labeled Potential GDP. A callout with an arrow to where AD and AS cross reads price level = 90, real GDP = 8,800, and a brace under the axis from Yₑ at 8,800 to Yf at 9,500 is labeled Recessionary gap
caption: An AD–AS graph drawn from a schedule of seven price levels, from 70 to 130, with the real GDP demanded and supplied at each, a dot at each row. AD and AS cross at a price level of 90 and real GDP of 8,800, written in a callout. Potential GDP stands at 9,500, and the recessionary gap of 700 between them is braced under the axis.

title: AD–AS graph of a recessionary gap closed by expansionary fiscal policy (AD shifts right)
description: AD–AS graph of price level against real GDP with no numbers on the axes: a vertical green LRAS line, an upward-sloping red SRAS line, and a blue AD₁ line crossing SRAS at a dot labeled E₁, to the left of LRAS; two arrows point right to AD₂, which crosses SRAS on LRAS at a dot labeled E₂. Dashed lines run from E₁ to both axes and from E₂ to the price level axis, marked PL₁ and PL₂ on the price level axis and Y₁ and Yf on the real GDP axis, and a brace under the axis from Y₁ to Yf is labeled Recessionary gap
caption: An economy in a recessionary gap brought to full employment by an increase in aggregate demand, drawn with no numbers, as AP graphs are. AD₁ and SRAS cross at E₁, at real GDP Y₁, short of full-employment output Yf where LRAS stands, and the gap between them is braced under the axis. AD shifts right to AD₂, which crosses SRAS on LRAS at E₂: real GDP rises to Yf and the price level rises from PL₁ to PL₂.

title: Business cycle graph: peak, trough, expansion and contraction
description: Business cycle graph with Real GDP up the side, Time along the bottom and no numbers on the axes: a blue wave of real GDP rising from a dashed, upward-sloping long-run trend line to a high point labeled Peak, falling to a low point labeled Trough, then rising to a second, higher Peak and turning down, with an arrow to the fall after the first peak labeled Contraction and an arrow to the rise before the second peak labeled Expansion
caption: Real GDP rising and falling over time around a dashed long-run trend that slopes upward, drawn with no numbers on the axes. Real GDP rises to a peak, falls to a trough, then rises to a second, higher peak and turns down again. Arrows label the fall after the first peak Contraction and the rise to the second peak Expansion.

title: Phases of the business cycle: expansion, peak, contraction, recession, trough and recovery
description: Business cycle graph with Real GDP up the side, Time along the bottom and no numbers on the axes: a blue wave of real GDP around a dashed, upward-sloping trend line, with two high points labeled Peak and a low point labeled Trough; on the fall after the first peak, an arrow from above labeled Contraction and an arrow from below labeled Recession; on the rise after the trough, arrows labeled Recovery near the trough and Expansion near the second peak; and an arrow up to the dashed line labeled Long-run trend
caption: Every term of the business cycle on one graph of real GDP over time. Real GDP rises to a peak, falls to a trough and rises to a second, higher peak, around a dashed line labeled Long-run trend. The fall is labeled both Contraction, from above, and Recession, from below, two names for the same phase, and the rise is labeled Recovery just after the trough and Expansion nearer the second peak.

title: Business cycle quiz: identify the phases at letters A to G
description: Business cycle graph with Real GDP up the side, Time along the bottom and no numbers on the axes: a blue wave of real GDP around a dashed, upward-sloping trend line, with letters A to G from left to right, A an arrow to the first rise, B a dot at the first peak, C an arrow to the fall after it, D a dot at the trough, E an arrow to the next rise, F a dot at the second peak and G an arrow to the fall at the end
caption: A business cycle for students to identify, lettered A to G from left to right instead of labeled. Dots mark the two peaks (B and F) and the trough (D), and arrows point to each rise (A and E) and each fall (C and G) of real GDP. The answer key reads A: Expansion, B: Peak, C: Contraction, D: Trough, E: Expansion, F: Peak and G: Contraction.

title: Business cycle graph with recessions shaded and irregular cycles
description: Business cycle graph with Real GDP up the side, Time along the bottom and no numbers on the axes: a blue wave of real GDP with three peaks and three troughs of different heights and spacing, each labeled Peak or Trough, each higher than the last as the dashed long-run trend rises, gray bands shading each fall from a peak to the next trough, an arrow to the first fall labeled Recession, an arrow to the rise before the second peak labeled Expansion, and an arrow down to the dashed line labeled Long-run trend
caption: Three irregular business cycles, each rise and fall a different size and length, around a dashed, upward-sloping long-run trend. Gray bands shade the recessions, from each peak down to the trough after it. Each peak and trough is labeled, along with one recession, one expansion and the long-run trend.

title: Business cycle worksheet: label the peaks, trough, expansion and contraction
description: Black and white business cycle graph with Real GDP up the side, Time along the bottom and no numbers on the axes: a wave of real GDP around a dashed, upward-sloping trend line, with a dot and a blank line above each of the two peaks, a dot and a blank line below the trough, and arrows with blank lines pointing to the fall after the first peak and to the rise before the second peak
caption: A worksheet business cycle in black and white, with blank lines for students to label. Real GDP rises to a peak, falls to a trough and rises to a second, higher peak around a dashed long-run trend. Dots mark the two peaks and the trough, each with a blank line, and arrows with blank lines point to the fall after the first peak and the rise to the second.

title: Cost curves graph: MC, ATC, AVC and AFC
description: Graph of Price and costs against Quantity with no numbers on the axes: a red MC curve that dips and then rises steeply, a U-shaped green ATC curve, a U-shaped purple AVC curve below it, and a dashed orange AFC curve falling all the way across. MC passes through the lowest points of AVC and ATC, each marked with a dot, and the gap between ATC and AVC narrows as quantity grows.
caption: A firm’s cost curves: marginal cost (MC), average total cost (ATC), average variable cost (AVC) and average fixed cost (AFC, dashed). MC falls, then rises through the lowest point of AVC and then the lowest point of ATC, each marked with a dot. AFC falls as output grows, so ATC and AVC, which are AFC apart, draw closer together.

title: Monopolistic competition long-run equilibrium graph with excess capacity
description: Graph of Price and costs against Quantity with no numbers on the axes: a downward-sloping demand curve D = AR just touching a U-shaped ATC curve at a dot, a dashed MR curve, and MC crossing MR directly below the dot. Dashed lines run from the dot to Pₑ on the price axis and qₑ on the quantity axis, and from a dot at the lowest point of ATC, where MC crosses it, down to q with the subscript min ATC. A brace under the quantity axis from qₑ to q min ATC is labeled Excess capacity.
caption: A monopolistically competitive firm in long-run equilibrium. It produces qₑ, where MR meets MC, and its demand curve just touches ATC there, so the price Pₑ equals ATC and the firm makes zero economic profit. qₑ is less than the quantity at ATC’s lowest point, and the gap between them is bracketed as excess capacity.

title: Monopoly graph with profit, consumer surplus and deadweight loss
description: Graph of Price and costs against Quantity with no numbers on the axes: a downward-sloping demand curve D = AR, a dashed marginal revenue curve MR twice as steep, and MC and ATC curves. A dot on demand above where MR meets MC, with dashed lines to PM on the price axis and QM on the quantity axis (the M a subscript). Shaded: a blue triangle labeled CS under demand above PM, a green rectangle labeled Profit between PM and a dashed line at ATC on the price axis, and an orange triangle labeled DWL between demand and MC from QM to where they cross.
caption: A monopoly producing QM, where marginal revenue meets marginal cost, and charging PM, read up from QM to the demand curve. The rectangle between PM and ATC out to QM is the monopoly’s profit, and the triangle under demand above PM is consumer surplus. The triangle between demand and MC, from QM out to where they cross, is the deadweight loss.

title: Regulated natural monopoly graph: socially optimal (P = MC) and fair-return (P = ATC) prices
description: Graph of Price and costs against Quantity with no numbers on the axes: demand D = AR, a dashed MR curve, and MC and ATC curves, ATC still falling where demand crosses MC. Three dots on demand, each with dashed lines to both axes: PM and QM above where MR meets MC; PFR and QFR where demand crosses ATC the second time; and PSO and QSO where demand crosses MC, the lowest price and the largest quantity (M, FR and SO subscripts).
caption: A natural monopoly, whose ATC is still falling where demand meets MC, at the three prices it could charge. Unregulated, it produces QM, where MR = MC, and charges PM. At the fair-return price PFR, where demand meets ATC, it produces QFR and breaks even; at the socially optimal price PSO, where demand meets MC, it produces the most, QSO, at a price below ATC.

title: Perfect competition short-run loss graph with blank labels (worksheet)
description: Graph of Price and costs against Quantity with no numbers on the axes and every label a blank line: red MC, green ATC and purple AVC curves, each with a blank at its end, and a blue horizontal price line with a blank, between the lowest points of AVC and ATC. MC meets the price line at a dot with a dashed line down to a blank on the quantity axis. A red rectangle with a blank inside lies between the price line and a dashed line at ATC, and the price and ATC each have a blank at the price axis. Arrows from two more blanks point to dots at the lowest points of AVC and ATC.
caption: A perfectly competitive firm making a short-run loss, with every label a blank line for students to fill in. The price line sits between the lowest points of AVC and ATC; the firm produces where the price line meets MC, and the shaded rectangle between the price and ATC out to that quantity is the loss. The blanks are for the four lines, the price, ATC and quantity at the axes, the loss, and the shutdown and break-even points.

title: Perfect competition side-by-side graphs: market and firm making an economic profit
description: Side-by-side graphs with no numbers on the axes. Left, labeled Market: supply S and demand D crossing at a dot, with dashed lines to Pₑ on the Price axis and Qₑ on the Quantity axis. The dashed line at Pₑ runs across to the right graph, labeled Firm, where it becomes the horizontal price line D = MR = AR = P. On the firm’s graph of Price and costs against Quantity, MC, ATC and AVC curves, MC meeting the price line at a dot above qₑ, a green rectangle labeled Profit between the price line and a dashed line at ATC on the price axis, and arrows to dots labeled Shutdown point, at the lowest AVC, and Break-even point, at the lowest ATC.
caption: A perfectly competitive market beside one of its firms. Market supply and demand set the price Pₑ, and the dashed line carries it across to the firm, where it is the horizontal line D = MR = AR = P. The firm produces qₑ, where MC meets the price line, and the shaded rectangle between the price and ATC out to qₑ is its economic profit. The shutdown point (the lowest AVC) and the break-even point (the lowest ATC) are marked where MC crosses them.

title: Loanable funds graph: crowding out from government deficit spending
description: Loanable funds market graph with no numbers on the axes, Real interest rate up the side and Quantity of loanable funds along the bottom: an upward-sloping supply curve labeled SLF (red), a downward-sloping demand curve DLF₁ (blue) and a second demand curve DLF₂ to its right, two arrows pointing right from DLF₁ to DLF₂, and dashed lines from both equilibria to r₁ and the higher r₂ on the vertical axis and to Q₁ and Q₂ on the horizontal axis
caption: The loanable funds market when the government borrows to cover a deficit. The demand for loanable funds increases from DLF₁ to DLF₂ along an unchanged supply curve SLF. The real interest rate rises from r₁ to r₂ and the quantity of loanable funds from Q₁ to Q₂, marked with dashed lines to both axes.

title: Ample reserves graph: the Fed lowers its administered rates
description: Market for reserves graph with no numbers on the axes, Policy rate up the side and Quantity of reserves along the bottom: a demand for reserves curve DR₁ (blue) flat at the top, sloping down, then flat along the bottom, a second curve DR₂ with both flat parts lower, its slope on the same line as DR₁’s, each curve named both at its flat top by the vertical axis and at the end of its flat bottom, two arrows pointing down from DR₁ to DR₂ on their flat parts, a vertical supply of reserves curve SR (red) crossing both flat bottoms, dashed lines across to PR₁ and the lower PR₂ on the vertical axis, and Q₁ under SR
caption: The market for reserves with ample reserves: the vertical supply of reserves SR crosses the flat bottom of the demand for reserves. When the Fed lowers its administered rates, the flat parts of the demand for reserves shift down from DR₁ to DR₂ while its slope stays where it is. The policy rate falls from PR₁ to PR₂ while the quantity of reserves stays at Q₁.

title: Limited reserves graph: an open-market purchase lowers the policy rate
description: Market for reserves graph with no numbers on the axes, Policy rate up the side and Quantity of reserves along the bottom: a demand for reserves curve DR (blue) flat at the top, sloping down, then flat along the bottom, a vertical supply of reserves curve SR₁ (red) crossing its sloping part and a second vertical curve SR₂ to the right, also on the slope, two arrows pointing right from SR₁ to SR₂, dashed lines across to PR₁ and the lower PR₂ on the vertical axis, and Q₁ and Q₂ under the two supply curves
caption: The market for reserves with limited reserves: the vertical supply of reserves crosses the sloping part of the demand for reserves DR. An open-market purchase adds reserves, shifting supply right from SR₁ to SR₂. The policy rate falls from PR₁ to PR₂ and the quantity of reserves rises from Q₁ to Q₂.

title: Money market graph: an increase in the money supply (open-market purchase)
description: Money market graph with no numbers on the axes, Nominal interest rate up the side and Quantity of money along the bottom: a downward-sloping money demand curve labeled MD (blue), a vertical money supply curve MS₁ (red) and a second vertical curve MS₂ to its right, with two arrows pointing right from MS₁ to MS₂, dashed lines across from where each crosses MD to i₁ and the lower i₂ on the vertical axis, and Q₁ and Q₂ under the two supply curves
caption: The money market after the money supply increases, as when the Fed buys bonds. The vertical money supply curve shifts right from MS₁ to MS₂, shown by two arrows, along the downward-sloping money demand curve MD. The nominal interest rate falls from i₁ to i₂, and the quantity of money rises from Q₁ to Q₂.

title: Money market graph worksheet: label an increase in money demand
description: Black and white money market graph with no numbers on the axes, Nominal interest rate up the side and Quantity of money along the bottom: a vertical money supply curve, a downward-sloping money demand curve and a second demand curve to its right, two arrows pointing right between the demand curves, dashed lines across to two interest rates on the vertical axis, and blank lines for students to write the name of each curve, both interest rates and the quantity
caption: A worksheet money market graph in black and white, with no numbers on the axes. Money demand shifts right, shown by two arrows, along a vertical money supply curve, and dashed lines run across to the old and new interest rates. Each curve, both interest rates and the quantity of money have a blank line for students to label.

title: Phillips curve: expansionary policy in the short run and the long run (A to B to C)
description: Phillips curve graph with no numbers on the axes: point A where the blue curve SRPC₁ crosses the vertical red LRPC; a black arrow up along SRPC₁ to point B, at lower unemployment and higher inflation; a second blue curve SRPC₂ above and to the right of SRPC₁, with two blue arrows from SRPC₁ to it; and a black arrow across from B to point C, where SRPC₂ crosses the LRPC. Dashed lines run from the points to the axes, labeled π₁ and π₂ on the inflation axis and u₁ and uₙ on the unemployment axis
caption: The economy starts at A, where the short-run Phillips curve SRPC₁ crosses the long-run Phillips curve (LRPC) at the natural rate uₙ, with inflation at π₁. It moves up along SRPC₁ to B, where unemployment has fallen to u₁ and inflation has risen to π₂. The SRPC then shifts up to SRPC₂, and the economy moves across to C on the LRPC, back at uₙ with inflation at π₂.

title: Numbered Phillips curve: contractionary policy and disinflation (A to B to C)
description: Phillips curve graph with numbered axes and gridlines, the unemployment rate numbered every 2% up to 14% and the inflation rate every 1% from −2% to 9%, the axes crossing at 0%: point A at 5% unemployment and 6% inflation, where the blue curve SRPC₁ crosses the vertical red LRPC at uₙ; a black arrow down along SRPC₁ to point B at 8% unemployment and 2% inflation; a lower blue curve SRPC₂ that falls below 0% inflation at higher unemployment, with a blue arrow down to it from SRPC₁; and a black arrow across from B to point C at 5% unemployment and 2% inflation. Dashed lines run to the axes, labeled π₁ at 6%, π₂ at 2%, uₙ at 5% and u₁ at 8%
caption: A Phillips curve graph on numbered axes, with percent signs on the numbers. The economy starts at A, 5% unemployment and 6% inflation, where the short-run Phillips curve SRPC₁ crosses the long-run Phillips curve (LRPC) at the natural rate of 5%. It moves down along SRPC₁ to B, 8% unemployment and 2% inflation, then the SRPC shifts down to SRPC₂ and the economy moves across to C, back at 5% unemployment with inflation at 2%. The inflation axis runs down to −2%, where SRPC₂ falls below 0% (deflation) at higher unemployment.

title: Short-run and long-run Phillips curve graph (SRPC and LRPC)
description: Phillips curve graph with no numbers on the axes, Inflation rate up the side and Unemployment rate along the bottom: a blue curve labeled SRPC sloping down and bending, flatter toward the right, crossing a vertical red line labeled LRPC at point A, with a dashed line across from A to the inflation axis, labeled π, and the LRPC meeting the unemployment axis at uₙ
caption: The short-run Phillips curve (SRPC) slopes down and bends, steep at low unemployment and flatter at high unemployment, and crosses the vertical long-run Phillips curve (LRPC) at point A. The LRPC stands at the natural rate of unemployment, labeled uₙ on the unemployment axis, and a dashed line runs across from A to the inflation rate π. The axes have no numbers, as AP Macroeconomics graphs are drawn.

title: Phillips curve shift after a negative supply shock (stagflation)
description: Phillips curve graph with no numbers on the axes: point A where the blue curve SRPC₁ crosses the vertical red LRPC; a second blue curve SRPC₂ above and to the right of SRPC₁, with two blue arrows from SRPC₁ to it; and a black arrow from A up and to the right to point B on SRPC₂, at higher unemployment and higher inflation. Dashed lines run from A and B to the axes, labeled π₁ and π₂ on the inflation axis and uₙ and u₁ on the unemployment axis
caption: A negative supply shock shifts the short-run Phillips curve to the right, from SRPC₁ to SRPC₂. The economy moves from A, on the long-run Phillips curve (LRPC) at the natural rate uₙ with inflation at π₁, to B on SRPC₂, where unemployment has risen to u₁ and inflation to π₂. Both are higher at once: stagflation.

title: Phillips curve worksheet: label the short-run and long-run adjustment
description: Black and white Phillips curve graph with no numbers, axes titled Inflation rate and Unemployment rate: two short-run Phillips curves sloping down and a vertical long-run Phillips curve; three points, one where the lower short-run curve crosses the vertical line, one up and to the left along that curve, and one where the upper curve crosses the vertical line; arrows from point to point and from the lower curve to the upper one; dashed lines to both axes; and a blank line for students to write each curve’s name, each point’s letter and the two inflation rates and two unemployment rates at the axes
caption: A worksheet version of the long-run adjustment graph, in black and white with no numbers on the axes. Two short-run Phillips curves, a vertical long-run Phillips curve, three points and dashed lines to the axes are drawn, with arrows from point to point and from one short-run curve to the other. Every curve name, point letter and rate at the axes is a blank line for students to fill in.

title: Comparative advantage: two countries’ production possibilities curves side by side
description: Two production possibilities graphs side by side on the same scale, each with cloth on the y-axis and wheat on the x-axis: under the first, Country A, a straight blue line labeled PPC from 20 cloth to 40 wheat; under the second, Country B, a straight red line labeled PPC from 30 cloth to 30 wheat, each number written where its line meets the axis
caption: Production possibilities curves for two countries making wheat and cloth, drawn side by side on the same scale. Country A (blue) can make 40 wheat or 20 cloth, and Country B (red) 30 wheat or 30 cloth. Each curve is a straight line between those amounts, which are written where it meets the axes.

title: PPC shifting outward: economic growth on a production possibilities curve
description: Two bowed-out production possibilities curves with capital goods on the y-axis and consumer goods on the x-axis and no numbers: the inner curve labeled PPC₁ with point A on it, the outer curve labeled PPC₂ with point B on it, and two arrows from the inner curve out to the outer one
caption: A production possibilities curve between consumer goods and capital goods shifting outward, from PPC₁ to PPC₂, drawn with no numbers on the axes. Two arrows point from the old curve out to the new one. Point A is on PPC₁, and point B is on PPC₂ above and to the right of it, with more of both goods.

title: Production possibilities curve with efficient, inefficient and unattainable points
description: Bowed-out production possibilities curve labeled PPC, with capital goods on the y-axis and consumer goods on the x-axis and no numbers: point A on the curve with an arrow from the caption Efficient, point B inside the curve with an arrow from the caption Inefficient, and point C outside the curve with an arrow from the caption Unattainable
caption: A production possibilities curve between consumer goods and capital goods, bowed out and drawn with no numbers on the axes. Point A is on the curve, captioned Efficient; point B is inside it, captioned Inefficient; and point C is outside it, captioned Unattainable. Each caption has an arrow to its point.

title: Increasing opportunity cost on a numbered production possibilities curve
description: Production possibilities curve on numbered axes with gridlines, capital goods on the y-axis from 0 to 140 and consumer goods on the x-axis from 0 to 110: a bowed-out curve labeled PPC from 120 capital goods to 100 consumer goods, with points A to E on it at 0, 25, 50, 75 and 100 consumer goods and 120, 110, 90, 60 and 0 capital goods, joined by dashed steps labeled −10 and +25, −20 and +25, −30 and +25, and −60 and +25
caption: A bowed-out production possibilities curve on numbered axes, meeting the capital goods axis at 120 and the consumer goods axis at 100. Points A to E sit on the curve at 0, 25, 50, 75 and 100 consumer goods, joined by dashed steps down and across. Each step gains 25 consumer goods and gives up more capital goods than the one before: 10, 20, 30 and then 60, written beside the steps.

title: Production possibilities curve worksheet: label the points (guns and butter)
description: Black and white production possibilities curve with guns on the y-axis and butter on the x-axis and no numbers: a bowed-out curve with points A and B on it, point C inside it and point D outside it, each with an arrow from a blank line for students to label, and a blank line beside the curve for its name
caption: A worksheet production possibilities curve between butter and guns, in black and white with no numbers on the axes. Points A and B are on the curve, point C is inside it and point D is outside it. Each point has an arrow from a blank line, for students to write whether it is efficient, inefficient or unattainable, and the curve has a blank line for its name.

title: Supply and demand graph: an increase in demand
description: Supply and demand graph with no numbers on the axes, Price up the side and Quantity along the bottom: a downward-sloping blue demand curve D₁ shifting right to D₂, with two arrows between them, and an upward-sloping red supply curve S. The equilibrium moves up along S from E₁ to E₂, each point with dashed lines to the axes labeled P₁ and P₂ on the price axis and Q₁ and Q₂ on the quantity axis
caption: An increase in demand on a schematic supply and demand graph. The demand curve shifts right from D₁ to D₂, shown by two arrows, while the supply curve S stays put. The equilibrium moves up along S from E₁ to E₂, and the dashed lines to the axes show the price rising from P₁ to P₂ and the quantity rising from Q₁ to Q₂.

title: Per-unit tax graph: tax incidence, tax revenue and deadweight loss
description: Supply and demand graph with no numbers on the axes, Price up the side and Quantity along the bottom: demand D and supply S crossing at E, and a dashed curve S + tax above S. Dashed lines mark Pb and Ps on the price axis, above and below Pₑ, the height of E, which has only a short dash at the axis, and Qt left of Qₑ on the quantity axis. Shaded regions are labeled CS in blue above Pb, Tax revenue in green between Ps and Pb out to Qt, PS in red below Ps, and DWL in orange, written above and right of the small triangle between Qt and Qₑ with an arrow to it
caption: A per-unit tax shifts the supply curve up from S to the dashed S + tax. Buyers now pay Pb, more than the price at the old equilibrium E, sellers keep Ps, less than it, and the quantity sold falls from Qₑ to Qt. The shaded areas show consumer surplus (CS), producer surplus (PS), the tax revenue between Ps and Pb, and the deadweight loss (DWL) between Qt and Qₑ.

title: Price ceiling graph: shortage and deadweight loss
description: Supply and demand graph with no numbers on the axes, Price up the side and Quantity along the bottom: demand D and supply S crossing at E, with dashed lines to Pₑ and Qₑ. A horizontal line labeled Price ceiling runs below Pₑ, with dots where it meets S and D and dashed lines down to Qs and Qd, a brace under it between them labeled Shortage, and a shaded triangle between the curves from Qs to Qₑ labeled DWL
caption: A binding price ceiling, set below the equilibrium price Pₑ. At the ceiling the quantity supplied Qs is less than the quantity demanded Qd, and the brace between them marks the shortage. The shaded triangle between the demand and supply curves, from Qs to the equilibrium quantity Qₑ, is the deadweight loss.

title: Supply and demand schedule graph with a price floor and surplus (numbered)
description: Numbered supply and demand graph titled Market for milk, Price ($/gallon) from 0 to 3.5 up the side and Gallons (thousands) from 0 to 900 along the bottom, with gridlines: demand D and supply S drawn through dots at each row of a schedule and crossing at E, with dashed lines to Pₑ at 2 and Qₑ at 600. A horizontal line labeled Price floor at 2.5 meets D at 500, marked Qd, and S at 700, marked Qs, with a brace above it between them labeled Surplus
caption: A supply and demand graph numbered from a schedule for the market for milk, with demand and supply plotted as dots at prices from $1 to $3 a gallon. The curves cross at an equilibrium price of $2 and a quantity of 600 thousand gallons. A price floor at $2.50 makes the quantity supplied, 700 thousand gallons, greater than the quantity demanded, 500 thousand, a surplus of 200 thousand gallons marked by the brace.

title: Supply and demand worksheet: label a decrease in supply
description: Black and white supply and demand graph with no numbers on the axes, Price up the side and Quantity along the bottom: a downward-sloping demand curve and an upward-sloping supply curve shifting left, with two arrows from the first supply curve to the second, and two equilibrium points with dashed lines to both axes. Every curve, point, price and quantity has a blank line for students to label
caption: A worksheet graph of a decrease in supply, in black and white with no numbers on the axes. The supply curve shifts left, shown by two arrows, and the equilibrium moves up along the demand curve to a higher price and a lower quantity. The curves, both equilibrium points and their prices and quantities at the axes are each left as a blank line for students to label.

title: Bar graph of favorite sports
description: A bar graph titled Favorite sports with a blue column for each of five sports over an axis from 0 to 10 titled Number of students
caption: A bar graph titled Favorite sports, with one blue column each for Soccer, Basketball, Swimming, Tennis and Running. The value axis is titled Number of students and numbered from 0 to 10 by 1, with light gridlines across it, and the sports are named under their columns above the title Sport. No values are written on the bars, so students read them from the axis.

title: Bar graph with a bar left for students to draw
description: A bar graph of rainfall from Monday to Friday with Thursday’s bar missing, over bold gridlines with minor lines for drawing it
caption: A bar graph of rainfall in millimeters from Monday to Friday with Thursday’s bar left off, so students draw it from a table or a description. Bold gridlines split into halves make the bar easy to draw to the nearest half millimeter, and the axis is titled Rainfall (mm).

title: Bar graph with error bars: mean plant height
description: A gray bar graph of mean plant height under three fertilizers, each bar with an error bar, and the note Error bars show ±1 SEM
caption: A bar graph of the mean height of plants given no fertilizer, fertilizer A and fertilizer B, in gray for printing, over an axis titled Mean height (cm). Each bar has an error bar with crossbars reaching one standard error of the mean above and below it, and the note under the graph says Error bars show ±1 SEM. Students judge whether the differences between the means are likely to be real.

title: Double bar graph: favorite pets of boys and girls
description: A double bar graph of favorite pets with a blue bar for boys and a red bar for girls beside each pet, and a key naming them
caption: A double bar graph of favorite pets, with two bars side by side for each of Dog, Cat, Fish and Rabbit: blue for Boys and red for Girls, named in a key on the right. The value axis is titled Number of students and numbered from 0 to 9. Students compare the two groups pet by pet.

title: Horizontal bar chart of books read, with values
description: A horizontal bar chart of books read by five students, each bar with its number written at its end
caption: A horizontal bar chart titled Books read this term, with a sideways bar for each of five students, Amara, Ben, Chen, Dana and Eli, named down the left. Each bar has its number of books written at its end, over an axis titled Books numbered from 0 to 12.

title: Stacked (composite) bar chart: how students travel to school
description: A stacked bar chart in black and white with a column for each of three year groups split into Walk, Bus and Car, and a key below
caption: A stacked bar chart, also called a composite bar chart, of how students in Years 7, 8 and 9 travel to school. Each year’s column is split into Walk, Bus and Car in gray, white and hatching, named in a key below the graph, with the number in each part written inside it. Black-and-white fills keep the parts apart on a photocopy.

title: Box plot from a five-number summary, with Q1, the median and Q3 labeled
description: A box plot over a number line from 10 to 40 with 18, 25 and 31 written above Q1, the median and Q3
caption: A box plot drawn from the five-number summary 12, 18, 25, 31, 40, over a number line from 10 to 40 numbered every 5. The values of Q1, the median and Q3, 18, 25 and 31, are written above the box; the whisker ends are left for students to read.

title: Box plot of test scores
description: A box plot of 15 test scores titled Test scores, over a number line from 60 to 100 labeled Score (points)
caption: A box plot of 15 test scores from 62 to 98, titled Test scores, over a number line from 60 to 100 numbered every 5 and titled Score (points). None of the five-number summary is written on it, so students read the minimum, quartiles, median and maximum from the line.

title: Box plot with outliers
description: A box plot of minutes spent on homework, with a dot for an outlier at each end beyond the whiskers
caption: A box plot of 13 students’ minutes spent on homework, titled Minutes spent on homework, over a number line from 0 to 80 numbered every 10. The two values more than 1.5 box widths past the box, 2 and 75, are drawn as dots of their own, and the whiskers stop at the last values that aren’t outliers.

title: Comparing two box plots: Class A and Class B
description: Two box plots, Class A above Class B, over one number line from 50 to 100 labeled Score
caption: Two box plots of ten test scores each, named Class A and Class B, drawn one above the other over the same number line from 50 to 100, with a tick every 5 and a number every 10. Sharing one line lets students compare the two classes’ medians, spreads and ranges straight down.

title: Parts of a box plot: label the five-number summary
description: A box plot with the letters A, B, C, D and E above its minimum, Q1, median, Q3 and maximum
caption: A box plot over a number line from 0 to 50 numbered every 5, with the letters A to E written above its minimum, Q1, median, Q3 and maximum. Students name the part each letter marks, or read its value from the line.

title: Alternate segment theorem: tangent and chord
description: A circle with a tangent at A and a triangle ABC inside it; the angle between the tangent and the chord AB is labeled 60° and the angle at C is labeled x
caption: A circle with a tangent touching it at A, at the bottom, and a triangle ABC with all three corners on the circle. The angle between the tangent and the chord AB is marked and labeled 60°, and the angle at C, in the alternate segment, is marked and labeled x.

title: Angle in a semicircle: a triangle on a diameter
description: A circle with diameter AB through its center O and a point C on the circle; triangle ABC has a right-angle square at C, the angle at B labeled 55° and the angle at A labeled x
caption: A circle with a diameter AB through its center O and a point C on the upper half. The chords CA and CB make a triangle on the diameter, with a right-angle square at C. The angle at B is marked and labeled 55° and the angle at A is marked and labeled x.

title: Angles in the same segment
description: A circle with points A and B at the bottom and C and D at the top; chords from C and from D to A and B make two angles on the same arc, the one at D labeled 70° and the one at C labeled x
caption: A circle with A and B on its lower part and C and D on its upper part. Chords run from C to A and B and from D to A and B, crossing in the middle, so the angles at C and D both stand on the arc AB. The angle at D is marked and labeled 70°, and the angle at C is marked and labeled x.

title: Central angle and inscribed angle on the same arc
description: A circle with center O and points A, B and C on it; radii OA and OB make a central angle labeled 120°, and chords CA and CB make an inscribed angle at C labeled x
caption: A circle with its center O and three points A, B and C on it. The radii OA and OB meet at O in a central angle marked with an arc and labeled 120°, and the chords CA and CB meet at C in an inscribed angle on the same arc AB, marked and labeled x, for the angle at the center is twice the angle at the circumference.

title: Cyclic quadrilateral: opposite angles
description: A quadrilateral ABCD with all four corners on a circle; the angle at C is labeled 95° and the opposite angle at A is labeled x
caption: A quadrilateral ABCD drawn inside a circle with all four corners on it, the circle’s center not shown. The angle at C is marked and labeled 95°, and the opposite angle at A is marked and labeled x, for the opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral.

title: Intersecting chords: the angle and its intercepted arcs
description: A circle with chords AB and CD crossing at E; arc AC is labeled 90°, arc BD is labeled 110°, and the angle AEC between them is labeled x
caption: A circle with two chords, AB and CD, crossing inside it at a point named E. The arc from C to A is labeled 90° and the opposite arc from D to B is labeled 110°, and the angle at E facing arc AC is labeled x, for the angle formed by two chords.

title: Parts of a circle: radius, diameter, chord, tangent and secant
description: A circle with center O, a diameter AB, a radius OC, a chord DE, a tangent touching the circle at F and a secant through G and H that runs on past both
caption: A circle with its center O and eight named points on it. A diameter runs from A through O to B, a radius from O to C, and a chord from D to E along the bottom. A tangent touches the circle at F, and a secant cuts through G and H and runs on past both, for naming the parts of a circle.

title: Regular hexagon inscribed in a circle
description: A regular hexagon ABCDEF inscribed in a circle with center O; every side has a tick, the radius OA is labeled 6 cm and the side AB is labeled x
caption: A regular hexagon ABCDEF with all six corners on a circle, its center O dotted. Every side is marked with one tick to show they are equal. The radius from O to A is labeled 6 cm and the side AB along the bottom is labeled x.

title: Shaded sector with its radius, central angle and arc length
description: A circle with center O and a shaded sector between radii OA and OB; OA is labeled 6 cm, the central angle 100° and the arc AB 10.5 cm
caption: A circle with its center O and a sector shaded blue between the radii OA and OB. The radius OA is labeled 6 cm, the central angle at O is marked with an arc and labeled 100°, and the arc from A to B is labeled with its length, 10.5 cm, for finding the sector’s area.

title: Shaded segment of a circle cut off by a chord
description: A circle with center O and a chord AB; the segment below the chord is shaded, dashed radii OA and OB meet at O at 140°, and OA is labeled 6 cm
caption: A circle with its center O and a chord AB across its lower part, with the segment between the chord and the circle shaded blue. Dashed radii run from O to A and B, OA labeled 6 cm, and the central angle between them is marked and labeled 140°, for finding the area of the segment.

title: Tangent and radius: find the angle
description: A circle with center O, a radius OA labeled 6 cm and a tangent touching the circle at A; the angle between the radius and the tangent is labeled x
caption: A circle with its center O and a radius from O to a point A on the circle, labeled 6 cm. A tangent touches the circle at A and runs on both ways, and the angle between it and the radius is labeled x with no right-angle mark, for the angle between a tangent and a radius.

title: Two secants from a point outside a circle
description: A circle and a point P outside it; two secants from P cut the circle at A and B and at C and D, the near arc AC is labeled 60°, the far arc BD 180°, and the angle at P x
caption: A circle and a point P outside it to the left. Two secants run from P through the circle, the upper one cutting it at A and then B, the lower one at C and then D. The near arc between A and C is labeled 60°, the far arc between B and D is labeled 180°, and the angle at P is marked and labeled x.

title: Two tangents from a point outside a circle
description: A circle with center O and a point P outside it; tangents from P touch the circle at A and B, each marked with a tick, radii OA and OB meet them at right angles, angle AOB is labeled 120° and angle APB is labeled x
caption: A circle with its center O and a point P outside it, two radii away from O. Two tangents run from P to the circle, touching it at A and B, each marked with one tick to show they are equal. The radii OA and OB meet the tangents at right angles, marked with squares; the angle AOB is labeled 120° and the angle APB is labeled x.

title: Cone with diameter 10 cm and slant height 13 cm
description: A cone with a dashed diameter across its base labeled 10 cm and its slant height labeled 13 cm
caption: A right cone with a diameter drawn dashed across its base and labeled 10 cm, and its sloping side labeled 13 cm. Its height is drawn dashed from the tip to the base with a right-angle square but isn’t labeled, for students to find.

title: Cone with radius 4 cm and height 9 cm
description: A cone with its dashed height labeled 9 cm and a dashed radius labeled 4 cm on its base
caption: A right cone drawn to scale, with its height drawn dashed from the tip down to the center of the base and labeled 9 cm, and a radius drawn dashed from the center to the edge and labeled 4 cm, with a right-angle square between them. The back of the base circle is dashed. Use it for volume.

title: Cone with radius r and height h
description: A cone with its dashed height labeled h and its radius labeled r, with no numbers
caption: A right cone labeled only with letters: its dashed height h and its radius r, with a right-angle square between them. Use it beside the volume formula V = ⅓πr²h, or on a formula sheet.

title: Cone with the slant height labeled x
description: A cone with its height labeled 8 cm, its radius 6 cm and its slant height x
caption: A right cone with its dashed height labeled 8 cm and its radius 6 cm, with a right-angle square between them, and its sloping side labeled x. Students use the Pythagorean theorem to find the slant height.

title: Graphs of y = 2ˣ and y = log₂ x, reflected in y = x
description: A coordinate grid from −6 to 6 with the exponential curve y = 2^x in blue, the logarithm curve y = log₂ x in red, and the dashed line y = x between them
caption: A coordinate grid numbered from −6 to 6 on both axes. The exponential curve y = 2ˣ is drawn in blue, passing through (0, 1) and (1, 2) and flattening toward the x-axis on the left; the logarithm y = log₂ x is drawn in red, passing through (1, 0) and (2, 1) and dropping toward the y-axis. The dashed line y = x between them shows that each is the other reflected, as inverse functions. Use it for inverses, domain and range, and asymptotes.

title: First-quadrant graph with axis titles: distance over time
description: A blank first-quadrant grid titled Distance over time, with Time (hours) along the x-axis from 0 to 10 and Distance (miles) up the y-axis from 0 to 100 by 10
caption: A blank first-quadrant grid with the chart title Distance over time. The x-axis is titled Time (hours) and numbered from 0 to 10 by 1; the y-axis is titled Distance (miles) and numbered from 0 to 100 by 10. Nothing is graphed, so students can plot a table of values or draw a line of best fit.

title: Graph of the parabola y = x² − 2x − 3
description: A coordinate grid from −6 to 6 with the upward parabola y = x² − 2x − 3 drawn in blue
caption: A coordinate grid numbered from −6 to 6 on both axes with the parabola y = x² − 2x − 3 drawn in blue. It opens upward, crosses the x-axis at −1 and 3, and has its vertex at (1, −4); both arms run off the top of the grid with arrowheads. Use it for questions on zeros, the vertex and the axis of symmetry.

title: Graph of y = 2x + 1 on a coordinate plane
description: A four-quadrant coordinate grid from −10 to 10 on both axes with the straight line y = 2x + 1 drawn across it
caption: A four-quadrant coordinate grid numbered from −10 to 10 on both axes, with arrows at every end and x and y at the arrow tips. The line y = 2x + 1 is drawn across it in black, crossing the y-axis at 1 and rising 2 for every 1 across, with an arrowhead where it leaves the grid at each end. The equation isn’t written on the figure, so students can find it from the graph.

title: Piecewise function graph with open and closed circles
description: A coordinate grid from −6 to 6 with a two-piece piecewise function: y = x + 2 for x < 1, ending in an open circle at (1, 3), and y = −2x + 4 for x ≥ 1, starting from a closed circle at (1, 2)
caption: A coordinate grid numbered from −6 to 6 on both axes with a piecewise function drawn in black. For x < 1 it’s the line y = x + 2, which ends in an open circle at (1, 3); for x ≥ 1 it’s the line y = −2x + 4, which starts from a closed circle at (1, 2). Use it for evaluating f(1), domain and range, or the jump at x = 1.

title: Plotting points in all four quadrants
description: A coordinate grid from −6 to 6 with four labeled points, A(2, 4), B(−3, 1), C(−4, −2) and D(5, −3), one in each quadrant
caption: A coordinate grid numbered from −6 to 6 on both axes, with four points drawn as dots and labeled with their letters only: A in the first quadrant, B in the second, C in the third and D in the fourth. Students read each point’s coordinates, or name the quadrant it’s in.

title: Rational function with a hole and dotted asymptotes
description: A coordinate grid from −6 to 6 with the rational function y = (2x² + 3x − 2)/(x² + x − 2) in green, an open circle for its hole at (−2, 5/3), and dotted asymptotes at x = 1 and y = 2
caption: A coordinate grid numbered from −6 to 6 on both axes with the rational function y = (2x² + 3x − 2)/(x² + x − 2) drawn in green. It factors as (2x − 1)(x + 2)/((x − 1)(x + 2)), so it has a hole at (−2, 5/3), drawn as an open circle, where x + 2 cancels; a vertical asymptote at x = 1 and a horizontal asymptote at y = 2, drawn as dotted lines, with the curve in two branches on either side. Use it for holes versus vertical asymptotes, limits and end behavior.

title: Graph of y = sin x from −2π to 2π
description: The sine curve y = sin x on a grid whose x-axis runs from −2π to 2π, numbered −2π, −π, 0, π and 2π, and whose y-axis runs from −2 to 2
caption: The curve y = sin x on a coordinate grid whose x-axis runs from −2π to 2π, with a gridline every π/2 and numbers at −2π, −π, 0, π and 2π, and whose y-axis runs from −2 to 2. The curve rises and falls between 1 and −1, crossing the x-axis at every multiple of π. The equation isn’t written on the figure.

title: System of linear inequalities: y > x − 2 and y ≤ −x + 3
description: A coordinate grid from −6 to 6 with the region above the dashed line y = x − 2 shaded blue and the region below the solid line y = −x + 3 shaded red, overlapping on the left
caption: A coordinate grid numbered from −6 to 6 on both axes with two inequalities shaded. Above the dashed line y = x − 2 is shaded blue, dashed because points on it don’t make y > x − 2 true; below the solid line y = −x + 3 is shaded red, solid because points on it make y ≤ −x + 3 true. The lines cross at (2.5, 0.5), and the solutions to the system are where the shading overlaps, to the left of that point.

title: Graph of y = 3 sin 2x in degrees, from 0° to 360°
description: The curve y = 3 sin 2x on a grid whose x-axis runs from 0° to 360°, with a gridline every 45° and numbers every 90°, and whose y-axis runs from −4 to 4
caption: The curve y = 3 sin 2x drawn in blue on a coordinate grid whose x-axis runs from 0° to 360°, with a gridline every 45° and numbers at 0°, 90°, 180°, 270° and 360°, and whose y-axis runs from −4 to 4. It goes through two full cycles, reaching 3 at 45° and 225° and −3 at 135° and 315°, so students can read its amplitude of 3 and period of 180°. The equation isn’t written on the figure.

title: Blank cumulative frequency graph axes
description: Blank cumulative frequency graph axes on graph paper, time from 0 to 60 minutes by 5 and cumulative frequency from 0 to 80 by 10
caption: A blank grid for a cumulative frequency graph, with dark gridlines each split into five smaller squares like graph paper. The horizontal axis is titled Time (minutes) and numbered from 0 to 60 by 5, and the vertical axis is titled Cumulative frequency and numbered from 0 to 80 by 10. Nothing is plotted, so students plot the points from a table and draw the curve.

title: Cumulative frequency curve from a data set of test marks
description: A cumulative frequency curve of 30 test marks with dashed red lines for the quartiles and median and three blank lines under the mark axis
caption: A cumulative frequency curve of 30 test marks, sorted into bins of 10 from 10 to 90, with crosses at each upper bound joined by a smooth blue curve. The mark axis runs from 10 to 90 by 10 and the cumulative frequency axis from 0 to 30 by 5. Dashed red lines go across from 7.5, 15 and 22.5 to the curve and down, each to a blank line under the axis for students to write the lower quartile, median and upper quartile.

title: Cumulative frequency curve with the median and quartiles
description: A cumulative frequency curve titled Heights of 80 students, with dashed red lines reading off the median, 169, and the quartiles, 162 and 177, written under the height axis
caption: A cumulative frequency curve titled Heights of 80 students, over a height axis from 140 to 200 cm by 5 and a cumulative frequency axis from 0 to 80 by 10. Crosses mark the running totals at each upper bound, starting from 0 at 140, joined by a smooth blue curve. Dashed red lines go across from 20, 40 and 60 to the curve and down, with the lower quartile 162, the median 169 and the upper quartile 177 written under the axis.

title: Cumulative frequency graph: estimate how many from the curve
description: A black-and-white cumulative frequency curve titled Weights of 120 parcels, with dashed lines for the median and up from 5 kg, and blank lines at the axes for the answers
caption: A cumulative frequency curve in black and white titled Weights of 120 parcels, over a weight axis from 0 to 12 kg by 1 and a cumulative frequency axis from 0 to 120 by 10, with crosses at 0 parcels for 0 kg, then 8, 30, 64, 96, 112 and 120 parcels every 2 kg up to 12. Dashed lines go across from 60 to the curve and down for the median, and up from 5 kg and across for how many parcels weigh 5 kg or less. A blank line under the weight axis and another left of the frequency axis are for students’ answers.

title: Cumulative frequency points for students to draw the curve
description: Crosses plotted for a cumulative frequency graph of time in minutes, from 0 to 60 on both axes, with no curve drawn through them
caption: Six crosses on a grid with dark gridlines split into halves: one at 0 minutes with a cumulative frequency of 0, then 5 at 10 minutes, 19 at 20, 40 at 30, 52 at 40 and 60 at 60. The time axis runs from 0 to 60 minutes and the cumulative frequency axis from 0 to 60, both by 5. No curve is drawn, so students join the points with a smooth curve.

title: Ogive of test scores with a cumulative percent axis
description: An ogive of test scores with dots joined by straight blue lines, a cumulative percent axis from 0 to 100, and dashed red lines across from 60 and down
caption: An ogive titled Test scores, with scores from 40 to 100 by 5 along the bottom and a cumulative percent axis from 0 to 100 by 10. Dots at 0% for 40, then 5%, 17.5%, 40%, 70%, 90% and 100% at each upper bound from 50 to 100, are joined by straight blue lines. Dashed red lines go across from 60% to the line and down to the score axis, with no value written, so students read the 60th percentile.

title: Cylinder with diameter 12 inches and height 9 inches
description: A cylinder with a diameter drawn across its top circle labeled 12 in, and its height labeled 9 in
caption: A right cylinder with a diameter drawn right across its top circle and labeled 12 in, and its height labeled 9 in. Students halve the diameter to find the radius.

title: Cylinder with radius 4 cm and height 10 cm
description: A cylinder with its radius drawn on the top circle and labeled 4 cm, and its height labeled 10 cm
caption: A right cylinder drawn to scale, with a radius drawn from the center of its top circle to the edge and labeled 4 cm, and its height labeled 10 cm up the side. The back half of the bottom circle is dashed. Use it for volume or surface area.

title: Cylinder with radius r and height h
description: A cylinder with its radius labeled r and its height labeled h, with no numbers
caption: A right cylinder labeled only with letters: its radius r, drawn from the center of the top circle, and its height h. Use it beside the volume formula V = πr²h, or on a formula sheet.

title: Oblique cylinder with its height and lean
description: An oblique cylinder leaning to the right with its radius labeled 3 cm, its dashed height 8 cm and its lean 4 cm
caption: An oblique cylinder leaning to the right, its top circle slid sideways past its base. Its radius is labeled 3 cm. The height is drawn dashed straight down from the top’s center to the base’s extended line, with a right-angle square, and labeled 8 cm, and the lean along that line is labeled 4 cm.

title: Frequency density histogram with unequal class widths
description: A gray histogram on graph paper with five bars of different widths for times from 0 to 50 minutes, over a frequency density axis from 0 to 3
caption: A GCSE-style histogram with unequal class widths: five gray bars for 0 < t ≤ 10, 10 < t ≤ 15, 15 < t ≤ 20, 20 < t ≤ 30 and 30 < t ≤ 50, so each bar’s area stands for its frequency. The vertical axis is titled Frequency density and numbered from 0 to 3 by 0.5, with each block split into fifths by minor gridlines, and the horizontal axis is titled Time (t minutes) and numbered at the bin edges 0, 10, 15, 20, 30 and 50.

title: Histogram from a data set of test scores
description: A histogram of 30 test scores in bins of 10 from 40 to 100, with each bar’s frequency written above it
caption: A histogram titled Test scores, drawn from a data set of 30 scores sorted into bins of 10 from 40 to 100. Each bar’s frequency is written above it: 2, 4, 6, 9, 6 and 3. The horizontal axis is titled Score, with a zig-zag break before 40, and the vertical axis is titled Number of students and numbered from 0 to 10.

title: Histogram of student heights
description: A histogram titled Heights of students with six touching blue bars over bins from 150 to 180 cm, with a zig-zag break on the horizontal axis before 150
caption: A histogram titled Heights of students, with six touching blue bars for the bins 150 ≤ h < 155 up to 175 ≤ h < 180. The horizontal axis is titled Height (cm) and numbered at the bin edges from 150 to 180, with a zig-zag break between the corner and 150. The vertical axis is titled Frequency and numbered from 0 to 11, and the tallest bar, 165 to 170, reaches 11.

title: Histogram with a bar left for students to draw
description: A histogram of distances from school with the bar for 10 to 15 km left off, on bold gridlines with minor lines
caption: A histogram of how far students live from school, with bars for the bins 0–5, 5–10, 15–20 and 20–25 km and no bar for 10–15 km, so students draw it from a frequency table. The vertical axis is titled Frequency and numbered from 0 to 12, on bold gridlines split into halves, and the horizontal axis is titled Distance from school (km).

title: Histogram with a frequency polygon
description: A histogram of the masses of apples with white bars from 100 to 200 g and a frequency polygon joining the middle of each bar’s top, closed down to the axis at each end
caption: A histogram titled Masses of apples, with five white bars for bins of 20 g from 100 to 200 g, and a frequency polygon drawn over them through the middle of the top of each bar. The polygon is closed down to the horizontal axis half a bin past each end, at 90 and 210 g. The vertical axis is titled Frequency and numbered from 0 to 16 by 2, and the horizontal axis, titled Mass (g), has a zig-zag break before 100.

title: Histogram with no numbers on the frequency density axis
