description: A histogram of masses from 20 to 70 kg with unequal bins and a frequency density axis with gridlines but no numbers
caption: A histogram of masses with five white bars of unequal width for 20 < m ≤ 30, 30 < m ≤ 35, 35 < m ≤ 40, 40 < m ≤ 50 and 50 < m ≤ 70 kg. The vertical axis is titled Frequency density but has no numbers, only gridlines, with each block split into fifths by minor ones, so students work out its scale from one bar’s frequency. The horizontal axis is titled Mass (m kg), with a zig-zag break before 20.

title: Kite: find the missing angle
description: A kite with short sides 6 and long sides 10, angle B labeled 110 degrees, equal angles A and C marked with arcs and angle D labeled x
caption: A kite ABCD with its short sides labeled 6 and marked with one tick, and its long sides labeled 10 and marked with two. ∠B at the top is labeled 110°, the two equal angles A and C are marked with one arc each, and ∠D at the bottom is labeled x.

title: Kite with diagonals 6 and 12 for area
description: A kite ABCD standing upright, its diagonals drawn and labeled 6 and 12, crossing at a right angle, with its equal sides marked
caption: A kite ABCD standing upright on its line of symmetry, its short sides marked with one tick and its long sides with two. Both diagonals are drawn: AC across is labeled 6 and BD down the middle 12, with a right-angle square where they cross and another at the top corner B. No side lengths are shown, so students find the area from the diagonals.

title: Kite with its line of symmetry
description: A kite with sides 7 in and 12 in and angle B 80 degrees, with the diagonal BD drawn dashed as its line of symmetry
caption: A kite ABCD with its short sides labeled 7 in and its long sides 12 in, each pair of equal sides marked with ticks, and ∠B labeled 80°. The diagonal BD from top to bottom is drawn dashed: the kite’s line of symmetry.

title: Measuring to the nearest centimeter
description: A 15 cm ruler marked only every centimeter with a row of four marbles lying along it from 0 to 6 cm
caption: A 15 cm ruler marked and numbered every centimeter, with no millimeter marks, and a row of four marbles lying along it from 0. Dashed lines drop from the row’s ends to the ruler, and its right end is on the 6 cm mark. There is no magnifier, so students read it from the whole ruler.

title: Measuring to the nearest eighth inch
description: A 6 inch ruler marked in eighths of an inch with a rock lying along it from 0 to 2 5/8 inches, with dashed lines down from its ends
caption: A 6 inch ruler marked every eighth of an inch, with marks shortening from halves to quarters to eighths, and a rock lying along it from 0. Dashed lines drop from the rock’s ends to the ruler, and its right end is on the 2 5/8 inch mark. A magnified view shows the right end against the marks.

title: Measuring to the nearest quarter inch
description: A 6 inch ruler marked in quarter inches with a metal cylinder lying along it from 0 to 3 1/4 inches, with a magnified view of its right end
caption: A 6 inch ruler marked every quarter inch, with longer marks at the half inches, and a metal cylinder lying along it with its left end on 0. Its right end is on the 3 1/4 inch mark. A magnified view shows the right end against the marks.

title: Measuring in centimeters and millimeters: 8.4 cm
description: A 15 cm ruler marked in millimeters with a metal cylinder lying along it from 0 to 8.4 cm, with a magnified view of its right end
caption: A 15 cm ruler marked every millimeter, with a longer mark at each half centimeter, and a metal cylinder lying along it from 0. Its right end is on the fourth millimeter mark past 8 cm, so it is 8.4 cm, or 84 mm, long. A magnified view shows the right end against the marks.

title: Measuring with a ruler not starting at zero, in inches
description: A 6 inch ruler marked in quarter inches with a metal cylinder lying along it from 1 inch to 3 1/2 inches, with magnified views of both ends
caption: A 6 inch ruler marked every quarter inch, with a metal cylinder lying along it from the 1 inch mark rather than 0. Magnified views show its left end on 1 inch and its right end on 3 1/2 inches, so students subtract to find its length.

title: Mapping diagram without arrows, for students to draw
description: A mapping diagram with inputs 1 to 5 titled x and outputs 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10 titled y, and no arrows
caption: A mapping diagram with the inputs 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 under the title x and the outputs 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10 under y, and no arrows between them. Students draw the arrows from a rule or a list of ordered pairs.

title: Mapping diagram of y = x², a function that isn’t one-to-one
description: A mapping diagram titled y = x² with inputs −2, −1, 1 and 2 and outputs 1 and 4, two arrows ending at each output
caption: A mapping diagram titled y = x², with the inputs −2, −1, 1 and 2 on the left, titled x, and the outputs 1 and 4 on the right, titled y. −2 and 2 both have arrows to 4, and −1 and 1 both have arrows to 1.

title: Mapping diagram of a function
description: A mapping diagram with inputs 1, 2, 3 and 4 in an oval on the left, outputs 3, 5, 7 and 9 on the right, and one arrow from each input
caption: A mapping diagram with the inputs 1, 2, 3 and 4 in an oval under the title Input and the outputs 3, 5, 7 and 9 in an oval under Output. One arrow goes from each input to one output: 1 to 3, 2 to 5, 3 to 7 and 4 to 9.

title: Mapping diagram of a relation that is not a function
description: A mapping diagram from x to y with inputs −2, 0 and 3, where 0 has arrows to both 4 and 6
caption: A mapping diagram of the ordered pairs (−2, 1), (0, 4), (0, 6) and (3, 8), with the inputs titled x and the outputs titled y. The input 0 has two arrows, one to 4 and one to 6.

title: Mapping diagram with words: students and their sports
description: A mapping diagram in boxes from four students, Ana, Ben, Cara and Dev, to three sports, with one arrow from each student
caption: A mapping diagram drawn in boxes, with four students, Ana, Ben, Cara and Dev, under the title Student and three sports, Soccer, Tennis and Swimming, under Sport. Ana and Cara both have arrows to Soccer, Ben to Tennis and Dev to Swimming.

title: Compound inequality −3 < x ≤ 4 on a number line
description: A number line from −6 to 6 with an open circle at −3, a closed circle at 4 and a thick line between them
caption: A number line from −6 to 6 with the compound inequality −3 < x ≤ 4 graphed on it: an open circle at −3, which isn’t included, a closed circle at 4, which is, and a thick line joining them. Every number between −3 and 4 makes it true.

title: Fraction number line from 0 to 2 with lettered points
description: A number line from 0 to 2 with a tick every quarter, numbered only at 0, 1 and 2, with points P, Q and R drawn as dots
caption: A number line from 0 to 2 with a tick every quarter, numbered only at the whole numbers 0, 1 and 2. Three points sit on ticks, drawn as dots and labeled only with their letters, P, Q and R, so students count the quarters and write the fraction each one stands for.

title: Graphing the inequality x ≥ −2 on a number line
description: A number line from −5 to 5 with a closed circle at −2 and a thick line with an arrow running right from it
caption: A number line from −5 to 5, numbered at every tick. The inequality x ≥ −2 is graphed on it: a closed circle at −2, because −2 is included, and a thick line from it running off the right end with its own arrow. The inequality itself isn’t written on the figure.

title: Graph of x < −1 or x ≥ 3 on a number line
description: A number line from −5 to 5 with an open circle at −1 and a thick line running left, and a closed circle at 3 with a thick line running right
caption: A number line from −5 to 5 with the “or” inequality x < −1 or x ≥ 3 graphed on it. An open circle at −1 has a thick line running off the left end, and a closed circle at 3 has one running off the right end, each with its own arrow. The numbers between −1 and 3 are left out.

title: The sequence aₙ = 1/n on a number line
description: A number line from 0 to 1 by tenths with the first five terms of 1/n drawn as dots at 1, 1/2, 1/3, 1/4 and 1/5
caption: A number line from 0 to 1, marked every tenth, with the first five terms of the sequence aₙ = 1/n drawn as dots: 1, 1/2, 1/3, 1/4 and 1/5. The terms bunch up as they near 0, which shows the sequence converging. Terms that don’t sit on a numbered tick have their value written above them.

title: Parallelogram: find the missing angles
description: A parallelogram with sides 9 and 5, angle A labeled 65 degrees and angles B, C and D labeled x, y and z
caption: A parallelogram ABCD with sides labeled 9 and 5 and ∠A labeled 65°. The other three angles are labeled x, y and z, with parallel arrows on both pairs of opposite sides, so students use what they know about a parallelogram’s angles to find each one.

title: Parallelogram with base and height for area
description: A parallelogram with base AB labeled 12 cm and a dashed height from D labeled 5 cm, with parallel arrows on opposite sides
caption: A parallelogram ABCD drawn to scale, its base AB labeled 12 cm. A dashed height drops from D to the base, labeled 5 cm, with a right-angle square where it lands. Parallel arrows mark AB and CD with one arrow, and BC and DA with two.

title: Rhombus with its diagonals drawn
description: A rhombus ABCD with side 6 and angle A 70 degrees, each side marked with one tick, its diagonals crossing at E with a right-angle square
caption: A rhombus ABCD with side AB labeled 6 and ∠A labeled 70°, all four sides marked with one congruence tick. Both diagonals are drawn and cross at E, with a right-angle square showing that they are perpendicular.

title: Blank circle for drawing a pie chart
description: A blank circle with its center marked and a radius drawn up to 12 o’clock, and a key of four pets with black-and-white fills
caption: A blank circle with a dot at its center and one radius drawn up to 12 o’clock, under a blank line for the title. A key on the right gives Dog gray, Cat white, Fish hatching and Rabbit dots, for students to draw and shade a pie chart from a table.

title: Circle graph of how students travel to school, with a key
description: A circle graph of how students travel to school, each sector labeled with its percent, and a key on the right naming them
caption: A circle graph titled How we get to school, with sectors for Walk, Car, Bus and Bike in blue, red, green and orange, clockwise from 12 o’clock. Each sector is labeled with its percent only, 35%, 30%, 25% and 10%, and a key on the right names the colors.

title: Complete the pie chart: favorite sports
description: A pie chart of the favorite sports of 60 students with only Soccer, 120°, and Basketball, 90°, drawn and the rest of the circle left empty
caption: A pie chart titled Favorite sports of 60 students with only two sectors drawn, clockwise from 12 o’clock: Soccer in blue, labeled 120°, and Basketball in red, labeled 90°. The other 150° of the circle is left as one empty sector, with a dot at the center, for students to complete.

title: Pie chart: find the missing angle x
description: A black-and-white pie chart of Red, 110°, Blue, 80°, Green, 100°, and Yellow, x°
caption: A black-and-white pie chart of four sectors, each labeled with its name and angle: Red 110°, Blue 80°, Green 100° and Yellow x°, with a dot at the center. Students find x from the angles around a point adding up to 360°.

title: Pie chart of favorite fruit with percents
description: A pie chart titled Favorite fruit with a colored sector for each of four fruits, each labeled with its name and percent
caption: A pie chart titled Favorite fruit, with its sectors running clockwise from 12 o’clock: Apples in blue, Bananas in red, Cherries in green and Grapes in orange. Each sector is labeled inside with its name and percent: 40%, 26.7%, 20% and 13.3%.

title: Pie chart with fractions: how Sam spends a day
description: A black-and-white pie chart of how Sam spends 24 hours, each sector labeled with its activity and its fraction of the day
caption: A black-and-white pie chart titled How Sam spends a day, with sectors in gray, white, hatching, dots, cross-hatching and back hatching for Sleep 3/8, School 1/4, Play 1/8, Homework 1/12, Meals 1/12 and Other 1/12. Each is labeled with its name and fraction of the day, inside its sector except Homework, which is labeled outside with a short leader line.

title: Cube with 6-inch edges
description: A cube with one edge labeled 6 in and its hidden edges dashed
caption: A cube with only its front bottom edge labeled, 6 in, since every edge of a cube is the same length. The edges round the back are dashed. Use it for volume or surface area.

title: Hexagonal prism with its apothem
description: A hexagonal prism with a side labeled 4 cm, its height 10 cm, and an apothem of 3.5 cm drawn on its top face
caption: A prism with a regular hexagon for its base, standing up, with the front bottom side labeled 4 cm and the height 10 cm. On the top face, the apothem runs from the center, drawn as a dot, to the middle of a side, with a right-angle square, and is labeled 3.5 cm. The hidden edges are dashed.

title: Rectangular prism 8 cm by 3 cm by 5 cm
description: A rectangular prism drawn to scale with its length labeled 8 cm, its width 3 cm and its height 5 cm, hidden edges dashed
caption: A rectangular prism (a box) drawn to scale, seen from a little above, with its length labeled 8 cm along the front, its width 3 cm along the side going back, and its height 5 cm up the left. The three edges round the back are dashed. Use it for volume or surface area.

title: Rectangular prism with a missing height x
description: A rectangular prism with its length labeled 12 ft, its width 4 ft and its height x
caption: A rectangular prism with its length labeled 12 ft and its width 4 ft, and its height labeled x. Give students the volume and ask for x.

title: Triangular prism with a right triangle base
description: A triangular prism lying on its side, its right triangle end labeled 6 cm, 8 cm and 10 cm, and its length 12 cm
caption: A triangular prism lying on its side, with a right triangle at its front end: the legs are labeled 6 cm and 8 cm, with a right-angle square between them, and the hypotenuse 10 cm. The prism’s length going back is labeled 12 cm, and its hidden edges are dashed.

title: Hexagonal pyramid with its apothem and height
description: A hexagonal pyramid with a base side labeled 4 cm, its dashed height 9 cm and the base’s apothem 3.5 cm
caption: A pyramid on a regular hexagon, with a base side labeled 4 cm and its height drawn dashed from the tip to the center of the base and labeled 9 cm. The base’s apothem runs from the center to the middle of the front side, with a right-angle square, and is labeled 3.5 cm. Hidden edges are left off.

title: Rectangular pyramid 8 cm by 6 cm with height 9 cm
description: A rectangular pyramid with base edges labeled 8 cm and 6 cm and its dashed height labeled 9 cm
caption: A rectangular pyramid with its base edges labeled 8 cm and 6 cm. Its height is drawn dashed from the tip straight down to the middle of the base, with a right-angle square, and labeled 9 cm. Hidden edges are dashed. Use it for volume.

title: Square pyramid with slant height 10 cm
description: A square pyramid with base edges labeled 12 cm and a dashed slant height of 10 cm down the front face
caption: A square pyramid with two base edges labeled 12 cm. The slant height is drawn dashed from the tip down the middle of the front face to the base edge, with a right-angle square, and labeled 10 cm; the height isn’t drawn. Hidden edges are dashed. Use it for surface area.

title: Rectangle 12 cm by 5 cm for area and perimeter
description: A rectangle ABCD drawn to scale, its bottom side labeled 12 cm and its right side 5 cm, with right-angle squares at the corners
caption: A rectangle ABCD drawn to scale, 12 cm long and 5 cm wide, with its length labeled along the bottom side AB and its width along the right side BC. Each corner has a right-angle square. The other two sides are left unlabeled for students to work out.

title: Rectangle with a diagonal labeled x
description: A rectangle 8 by 6 with diagonal AC drawn and labeled x
caption: A rectangle ABCD drawn to scale, with its sides labeled 8 and 6 and a right-angle square at each corner. Diagonal AC is drawn from the bottom left corner to the top right and labeled x, for a Pythagorean theorem question.

title: Rectangle with sides labeled 2x + 3 and x
description: A rectangle with its length labeled 2x + 3 and its width labeled x
caption: A rectangle ABCD whose length AB is labeled 2x + 3 and whose width BC is labeled x, with right-angle squares at its corners. Use it for writing expressions for perimeter and area, or for solving for x given one of them.

title: Square with its diagonals drawn
description: A square ABCD with every side marked with one tick, its diagonals AC and BD crossing at E with a right-angle square
caption: A square ABCD with a side of 7, each side marked with one congruence tick. Both diagonals are drawn and cross at a point named E, with a right-angle square there and at every corner, showing that a square’s diagonals are perpendicular.

title: Regular decagon with congruence marks
description: A regular decagon with one tick mark on every side and an arc in every corner, and no numbers
caption: A regular decagon, 10 sides, with a congruence tick on every side and a congruence arc in every corner, showing that all its sides and all its angles are equal. Nothing is labeled with a number, so students can name the polygon or work out its angle sum.

title: Regular hexagon with its apothem, for area
description: A regular hexagon with its bottom side labeled 10 cm and a dashed apothem from the center dot to that side labeled 8.7 cm
caption: A regular hexagon with its center marked by a dot. The bottom side is labeled 10 cm, and a dashed apothem runs from the center to the middle of that side, labeled 8.7 cm, with a right-angle square where it meets the side. Students use the apothem and perimeter to find the area.

title: Regular octagon split into triangles by its radii
description: A regular octagon with a dashed radius from its center dot to each of its eight corners, one of them labeled 5
caption: A regular octagon with a dot at its center and a dashed radius to each of its eight corners, splitting it into eight matching triangles. The radius to the bottom right corner is labeled 5. Use it for central angles, or to find the area from the triangles.

title: Regular pentagon: find the interior angle
description: A regular pentagon with its bottom side labeled 6 and the angle in its bottom left corner marked with an arc and labeled x
caption: A regular pentagon with its bottom side labeled 6. The interior angle in its bottom left corner is marked with an arc and labeled x, for students to find from the number of sides. No center or other lines are drawn.

title: Hemisphere bowl with radius 8 cm
description: A hemisphere with its flat face up, like a bowl, and a radius across its top labeled 8 cm
caption: A hemisphere with its flat face up, like a bowl, and a radius drawn from the center of the top circle to its edge, labeled 8 cm. Use it for how much a bowl holds.

title: Hemisphere with radius 5 m
description: A hemisphere with its flat face down, like a dome, and a radius on its flat face labeled 5 m
caption: A hemisphere with its flat face down, like a dome. The back of the flat face’s circle is dashed, and a radius is drawn from its center to the edge and labeled 5 m.

title: Sphere with diameter 14 inches
description: A sphere with a diameter drawn right across its middle and labeled 14 in
caption: A sphere with a circle round its middle, the back half dashed, and a diameter drawn right across it through the center, labeled 14 in. Students halve it to find the radius.

title: Sphere with radius 6 cm
description: A sphere with a radius drawn from its center to its edge and labeled 6 cm
caption: A sphere with a circle round its middle, the back half dashed, and a radius drawn from the center, shown as a dot, to the edge and labeled 6 cm. Use it for volume or surface area.

title: Back-to-back stem-and-leaf plot: Class A and Class B
description: A back-to-back stem-and-leaf plot titled Push-ups in one minute, with Class A’s leaves running left and Class B’s running right from shared stems 2 to 5
caption: A back-to-back stem-and-leaf plot titled Push-ups in one minute, comparing Class A and Class B. The stems 2, 3, 4 and 5 run down the middle between two lines, with Class A’s leaves running left from them and Class B’s running right, each in order outward from the stem and headed with its class’s name. The key reads 4 | 2 | 1 means 24 for Class A and 21 for Class B. Students compare the two classes’ medians and ranges.

title: Blank stem-and-leaf diagram with boxes to fill in
description: A blank stem-and-leaf diagram with the stems 1 to 5, a row of eight empty boxes for leaves beside each, and the key 2 | 3 means 23 minutes
caption: A blank stem-and-leaf diagram for students to fill in from a list of data, with the stems 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 down the left and a row of eight empty boxes beside each for the leaves. The key reads 2 | 3 means 23 minutes, and the title is Time to finish a puzzle.

title: Stem-and-leaf plot of test scores
description: A stem-and-leaf plot titled Test scores with stems 5 to 9, the leaves in order, and the key 5 | 8 = 58
caption: A stem-and-leaf plot titled Test scores, with the headings Stem and Leaf. The stems 5, 6, 7, 8 and 9 run down the left of a line, and each score’s last digit is written in order across its stem’s row, from 5 | 8 for 58 up to 9 | 0 2 7. The key under the plot reads 5 | 8 = 58. Students find the median, mode and range from it.

title: Stem-and-leaf plot with decimals: plant heights in cm
description: A stem-and-leaf plot titled Plant heights with whole-number stems 1 to 4, tenths as leaves, and the key 1 | 4 means 1.4 cm
caption: A stem-and-leaf plot titled Plant heights, of heights in centimeters measured to the nearest tenth. The whole numbers 1, 2, 3 and 4 are the stems and the tenths are the leaves, so 2 | 6 stands for 2.6 cm. The key reads 1 | 4 means 1.4 cm.

title: Stem-and-leaf plot with negative stems: temperatures
description: A stem-and-leaf plot titled Daily low temperatures with the stems −1, −0, 0 and 1, and the key −0 | 5 = −5 °C
caption: A stem-and-leaf plot titled Daily low temperatures, of temperatures in degrees Celsius from −12 °C to 15 °C. The stems run −1, −0, 0 and 1 from the coldest to the warmest, with −0 holding −1 to −9 and 0 holding 0 to 9, and a negative stem’s leaves written so the values rise across its row. The key reads −0 | 5 = −5 °C.

title: Stem-and-leaf plot with split stems
description: A stem-and-leaf plot titled Ages of club members with each of the stems 3, 4 and 5 on two rows, leaves 0 to 4 on the first and 5 to 9 on the second, and the key 3 | 1 = 31
caption: A stem-and-leaf plot titled Ages of club members, with split stems: each of the stems 3, 4 and 5 takes two rows, the first for leaves 0 to 4 and the second for leaves 5 to 9, which spreads out data crowded onto a few stems. The key reads 3 | 1 = 31.

title: Isosceles trapezoid with bases and height for area
description: An isosceles trapezoid with bases 14 cm and 8 cm, a dashed height of 4 cm, parallel arrows on the bases and a tick on each leg
caption: An isosceles trapezoid ABCD drawn to scale, with its bases labeled 14 cm along the bottom and 8 cm along the top, each marked with a parallel arrow. A dashed height from D to the bottom base is labeled 4 cm, and the two equal legs are each marked with one congruence tick.

title: Isosceles trapezoid with its diagonals drawn
description: An isosceles trapezoid with bases 12 and 6, both diagonals drawn and crossing at E, with a tick on each leg
caption: An isosceles trapezoid ABCD with its bases labeled 12 and 6 and marked parallel, each leg marked with one congruence tick. Both diagonals are drawn and cross at a point named E. There is no height or other label, so students can show the diagonals are the same length.

title: Right trapezoid: find the slanted side
description: A right trapezoid with bases 15 and 9, a vertical leg of 8 and the slanted leg labeled x
caption: A right trapezoid ABCD with its bases labeled 15 along the bottom and 9 along the top, marked parallel with one arrow each. The left leg DA is labeled 8 and meets both bases at right angles; the slanted leg BC is labeled x.

title: Trapezoid with an angle and its height
description: A trapezoid with bases 12 and 6, a dashed height of 5, angle A labeled 60 degrees and angle D labeled x
caption: A trapezoid ABCD with its bases labeled 12 and 6, marked parallel with one arrow each, and a dashed height of 5 dropped from D. ∠A is labeled 60° and ∠D is labeled x, for a question on the angles along a leg between parallel lines.

title: 30-60-90 triangle with hypotenuse 10
description: Right triangle ABC with a 30° angle at A, a right angle at B, the hypotenuse labeled 10 and the legs labeled x and y
caption: A 30-60-90 right triangle ABC drawn to scale, with the 30° angle at A marked and labeled and a right-angle square at B. The hypotenuse is labeled 10, the short leg BC, across from the 30° angle, is labeled x, and the long leg AB is labeled y.

title: Isosceles triangle with its height drawn, for area
description: Isosceles triangle ABC with base AB labeled 10, equal sides CA and BC labeled 13 with one tick mark each, and a dashed height from C labeled h
caption: An isosceles triangle ABC with base AB labeled 10 and its two equal sides, CA and BC, each labeled 13 and marked with a congruence tick. A dashed height runs from C down to the middle of AB, labeled h, with a right-angle square where it meets the base. Students find h, then the area.

title: Law of cosines: two sides and the angle between them
description: Triangle ABC with AB labeled 8 m, CA labeled 11 m, the 40° angle between them at A, and the third side BC labeled x
caption: A triangle ABC drawn to scale with two sides and the angle between them given: AB is 8 m, CA is 11 m and ∠A is 40°, marked with an arc. The third side, BC, is labeled x. There is no right angle, so students use the law of cosines.

title: Right triangle with legs 3 and 4: find the hypotenuse
description: Right triangle ABC with the right angle at B, leg AB labeled 3, leg BC labeled 4 and the hypotenuse CA labeled x
caption: A right triangle ABC drawn to scale, with a right-angle square at B. The legs are labeled with their lengths, 3 along the bottom (AB) and 4 up the side (BC), and the hypotenuse CA is labeled x. Use it for the Pythagorean theorem.

title: SOHCAHTOA: find the side opposite a 35° angle
description: Right triangle ABC with a 35° angle at A, a right angle at B, the hypotenuse labeled 12 cm and the side opposite A labeled x
caption: A right triangle ABC with a 35° angle at A and a right-angle square at B. The hypotenuse CA is labeled 12 cm and the side BC, opposite the 35° angle, is labeled x; the side AB next to it has no label. Students pick sine to find x.

title: Blank two-way table to complete from a description
description: A blank two-way table of adults and children choosing vanilla, chocolate or strawberry ice cream, with only the grand total of 60 given
caption: A two-way table with rows for adults and children and columns for vanilla, chocolate and strawberry ice cream, plus a Total column and Total row. Every cell is blank except the grand total, 60, and a blank line above the table is left for its title. Students fill it in from a description, such as “25 of the 60 people are adults”.

title: Conditional relative frequency table: favorite sport by grade, in row percents
description: A relative frequency table of favorite sport in grades 6, 7 and 8 as percents of each row, with lines only under the headings and before the totals
caption: A two-way table of the favorite sport of students in grades 6, 7 and 8, soccer, basketball or swimming, written as percents of each row: grade 6 is 50%, 30% and 20%, so each row’s total is 100%. The Total row gives each sport’s share of all students, 40%, 40% and 20%. Plain headings and lines only under the headings and before the totals give it a textbook look.

title: Joint relative frequency table: pets by grade
description: A two-way relative frequency table of grade 7 and grade 8 students with and without a pet, each cell a decimal of the grand total
caption: A joint relative frequency table of grade 7 and grade 8 students who have a pet or don’t. Each cell is its count divided by the grand total of 80, written as a decimal to two places: 0.35, 0.15, 0.30 and 0.20. The totals are the marginal relative frequencies, 0.50 for each grade, 0.65 with a pet and 0.35 without, and the grand total is 1.00.

title: Relative frequency table as fractions: left- and right-handed students
description: A two-way table of left- and right-handed boys and girls as fractions of each column, with the corner split by a diagonal into Hand and Student
caption: A two-way table of left- and right-handed boys and girls, each cell written as a fraction of its column’s total in lowest terms: 4/7 of the left-handed students are boys and 3/7 girls, 26/53 of the right-handed students are boys and 27/53 girls. The Total column shows each group is 1/2 of all 60 students. The corner is split by a diagonal, with Hand across the top and Student down the side.

title: Two-way table gap-fill: boys’ and girls’ language choices
description: A two-way table of the language 100 boys and girls chose, French, German or Spanish, with five cells left blank, totals included
caption: A two-way table of the language chosen by boys and girls, French, German or Spanish, with a Total column and Total row and a grand total of 100. Five cells are blank, two of them totals: the boys’ German and total, the girls’ French and Spanish, and the Spanish total. Students fill them in from the rows and columns that have only one gap, then the ones those open up.

title: Two-way table: how students travel to school, with gaps to fill
description: A two-way table of how students in Years 7, 8 and 9 travel to school by walking, bus or car, with totals and three cells left blank
caption: A two-way table titled How students travel to school, with Year down the side (Years 7, 8 and 9) and Transport across the top (Walk, Bus and Car), and a Total column and Total row. Every total is given, grand total 87, and one count in each row is left blank: Year 7 by bus, Year 8 by car and Year 9 walking. Students work each one out from its row or column.

title: Two-way table with an unknown, x
description: A two-way table of school lunches and packed lunches in Years 10 and 11, with one count written as x and the Year 11 total left blank
caption: A two-way table of how many students in Years 10 and 11 have a school lunch or a packed lunch, with totals. The Year 10 packed lunches are written as x, in italics, and the Year 11 total is left blank. Students find x from the Packed lunch column, then the missing total.

title: Prime factor Venn diagram for the HCF and LCM of 36 and 60
description: A Venn diagram of the prime factors of 36 and 60, with 2, 2 and 3 in the overlap, 3 in the 36 circle only and 5 in the 60 circle only
caption: Two overlapping circles named 36 and 60, in a box with no universal set symbol, holding the prime factors of each number: 36 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 3 and 60 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 5. The factors they share, 2, 2 and 3, are in the overlap, the other 3 is in 36 only, and 5 is in 60 only. Students find the HCF and LCM of 36 and 60 from it.

title: Three-set Venn diagram with numbers: pets
description: A three-set Venn diagram of Cat, Dog and Fish in a box marked U, with a number in each of its eight regions
caption: Three overlapping circles named Cat, Dog and Fish inside a box marked U, with the number of students owning each mix of pets in every region: 9 cat only, 7 dog only, 3 fish only, 4 cat and dog only, 2 cat and fish only, 1 dog and fish only, 2 all three, and 5, in the lower right corner, none of them.

title: Venn diagram with numbers: football and tennis
description: A Venn diagram of two overlapping circles, Football and Tennis, in a box marked U, with 12 in Football only, 5 in both, 8 in Tennis only and 15 outside
caption: Two overlapping circles named Football and Tennis inside a box marked U for the universal set, with the number of students in each region: 12 play football only, 5 play both, 8 play tennis only, and 15, written outside the circles in the lower left corner, play neither. Students read off totals, such as how many play football, or probabilities.

title: Venn diagram of probabilities: find x
description: A Venn diagram of probabilities with 0.3 in A only, x in the overlap of A and B, 0.25 in B only and 0.15 outside both circles
caption: Two overlapping circles named A and B inside a box marked U, with a probability in each region: 0.3 in A only, the unknown x in the overlap, 0.25 in B only, and 0.15 outside both circles in the lower right corner. Students find x, then probabilities such as P(A ∪ B).

title: Venn diagram with A ∩ B′ shaded
description: A Venn diagram of two overlapping circles, A and B, in a box marked U, with the part of A outside B hatched and nothing written in the regions
caption: Two overlapping circles named A and B inside a box marked U, with the region in A but not in B, A ∩ B′, shaded with diagonal hatching that photocopies well. Nothing is written in the regions, so students write the set notation for the shaded region.

title: Venn diagram sorting the numbers 1 to 20: even numbers and multiples of 3
description: A Venn diagram sorting the numbers 1 to 20 into two overlapping circles, Even and Multiples of 3, with the numbers in neither outside the circles
caption: The numbers 1 to 20 sorted into two overlapping circles named Even and Multiples of 3, inside a box marked U. 2, 4, 8, 10, 14, 16 and 20 are in Even only; 6, 12 and 18 are in both; 3, 9 and 15 are in Multiples of 3 only; and 1, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17 and 19 are outside both circles, in the lower right corner.

title: GCSE series circuit: a cell, a switch and two lamps
description: A circuit diagram in IEC symbols: a cell, a closed switch and two lamps L_1 and L_2 in series, with a voltmeter across L_1
caption: A circuit drawn in IEC symbols, as UK GCSE uses: one cell, a closed switch and two filament lamps, L_1 and L_2, in series, each lamp a circle with a cross. A voltmeter is connected across L_1. No values are given.

title: Parallel circuit with three resistors: find the unknown resistance
description: A circuit diagram of a 12 V battery with an ammeter reading 6 A, and three resistors in parallel: R_1 4 Ω, R_2 6 Ω and R_3 x
caption: A 12 V battery and an ammeter reading 6 A in the main line, with three resistors in parallel: R_1 of 4 Ω, R_2 of 6 Ω and R_3, whose resistance is the unknown x for students to find. The battery’s + and − terminals are marked.

title: Parallel circuit with two resistors and a voltmeter
description: A circuit diagram of a 6 V battery and an ammeter beside it, driving R_1 3 Ω and R_2 6 Ω in parallel, with a voltmeter across R_2 and its reading left blank
caption: A 6 V battery and an ammeter in the main line, with two resistors in parallel as the rungs of a ladder: R_1 of 3 Ω and R_2 of 6 Ω. A voltmeter is connected across R_2 with a blank reading, and junction dots mark where the branches meet.

title: Series circuit with two bulbs and an open switch
description: A circuit diagram of a 3 V battery, an open switch and two bulbs in series
caption: A 3 V battery, an open switch and two light bulbs in series, the bulbs drawn as circles with a looped filament. With the switch open, no current flows and neither bulb lights.

title: Series circuit with three resistors and an ammeter
description: A circuit diagram of a 12 V battery, an ammeter with a blank reading, and resistors R_1 2 Ω, R_2 4 Ω and R_3 6 Ω in series
caption: A 12 V battery of two cells drives one loop through three resistors in series, R_1 of 2 Ω, R_2 of 4 Ω and R_3 of 6 Ω, and an ammeter. The ammeter’s reading is a blank line for students to work out. Resistors are drawn as US zigzags.

title: Free body diagram of a block sliding down an incline with friction
description: A free body diagram of a block with F_g straight down, F_N tilted 30° from the vertical and marked θ, and F_f pointing up the slope, with a dashed velocity arrow down the slope
caption: A block sliding down a ramp that rises to the right at 30°, drawn without the ramp. Gravity F_g points straight down; the normal force F_N points up and to the left, square to the slope, with an angle mark θ between it and the dashed vertical; friction F_f points up the slope. A dashed velocity arrow v points down the slope.

title: Free body diagram of a box pushed across a floor with friction
description: A free body diagram of a block with four forces: F_g down, F_N up, F_A to the right and a shorter F_f to the left, with a dashed velocity arrow v to the right
caption: A block with four forces drawn from its middle: gravity F_g straight down, the normal force F_N straight up, an applied force F_A to the right and a shorter friction force F_f to the left. A dashed velocity arrow v beside the block points to the right, the way the box slides. There is no floor or hand in the figure, only the forces on the box.

title: Free body diagram of a falling ball with air resistance
description: A free body diagram of a ball with a long F_g arrow down and a shorter F_air arrow up, beside dashed v and a arrows pointing down
caption: A ball falling through the air, with gravity F_g straight down and a shorter air resistance force F_air straight up. Beside it, dashed arrows show its velocity v and acceleration a, both pointing down.

title: Free body diagram with the normal force and tension both pointing up, in vector notation
description: A free body diagram of a block with F_g straight down and two shorter arrows side by side pointing up, F_N and T, every label with an arrow over its letter
caption: A block resting on a floor while a rope pulls up on it, too weakly to lift it. Gravity F_g points straight down; the normal force F_N and the tension T both point straight up, drawn side by side and each shorter than F_g. Every label has an arrow over its letter, the way vectors are written.

title: Free body diagram of a sign hanging from two cables
description: A free body diagram of a dot with tensions T_1 and T_2 pulling up and out at θ above the horizontal on each side, and F_g straight down
caption: A dot with three forces: tensions T_1 up and to the left and T_2 up and to the right, each 30° above the horizontal and marked θ from a dashed horizontal line, and the weight F_g straight down. All three are drawn the same length.

title: Free body diagram of a sled pulled at an angle
description: A free body diagram of a block pulled by F_A at θ above the horizontal, with F_g down, a shorter F_N up and F_f to the left
caption: A block pulled by a rope, with the applied force F_A pointing up and to the right at 35° above the horizontal, its angle marked θ from a dashed horizontal line. Gravity F_g points down, friction F_f to the left, and the normal force F_N up, drawn shorter than F_g.

title: Ball on a ramp with its length, height and angle labeled
description: A ball labeled m on a ramp, with the slope’s length marked L, the ramp’s height marked h and its angle marked θ
caption: A ball labeled m on a smooth ramp rising to the right at 25°. The length of the slope is marked L along it, the ramp’s height is marked h beside its tall side, and the angle at the foot is marked θ. Use it for energy questions, such as the ball’s speed at the bottom.

title: Block on a rough inclined plane with gravity, normal force and friction
description: A block labeled m on a hatched ramp at angle θ, with F_g straight down, F_N out of the slope and F_f up the slope
caption: A block labeled m resting on a ramp that rises to the right at 30°, its angle marked θ at the foot. The slope is hatched to show it is rough. Gravity F_g points straight down from the block, the normal force F_N points out of the slope, and friction F_f points up the slope along the bottom of the block.

title: Block pushed up a rough incline with an applied force
description: A block labeled m on a rough ramp at θ, with F_A up the slope, F_f down the slope, F_g down and F_N out of the slope, and a dashed velocity v up the slope
caption: A block labeled m pushed up a rough ramp at 30°, its angle marked θ. The applied force F_A points up the slope and friction F_f points down it, opposing the motion; gravity F_g points straight down and the normal force F_N out of the slope. A dashed velocity arrow v points up the slope.

title: Cart rolling down a 20° ramp
description: A cart labeled m on a smooth ramp at 20°, with dashed velocity v and acceleration a arrows pointing down the slope
caption: A cart labeled m on a smooth ramp rising to the right, its angle labeled 20° at the foot. Dashed arrows above the cart show its velocity v and acceleration a, both pointing down the slope. No forces are drawn, so students can add them.

title: Label the forces: 5 kg block on a 35° incline
description: A block labeled 5 kg on a rough ramp at 35°, with three force arrows, down, out of the slope and up the slope, each with a blank line for its label
caption: A block labeled 5 kg on a rough, hatched ramp at 35°. Three force arrows are drawn from the block, straight down, out of the slope and up the slope, each with a blank line where its name goes, for students to label gravity, the normal force and friction.

title: Two blocks tied by a string, pulled up an incline
description: Blocks m_1 and m_2 on a ramp at θ, tied by a string, with F_A pulling m_2 up the slope, tension T at both ends of the string, F_g1 and F_g2 down and F_N1 and F_N2 out of the slope
caption: Two blocks on a smooth ramp at 30°, its angle marked θ: m_1 lower down and m_2 above it, tied together by a string parallel to the slope. An applied force F_A pulls m_2 up the slope, and tension T is drawn at both ends of the string, pulling each block toward the other. Each block has its own weight, F_g1 and F_g2, straight down, and its own normal force, F_N1 and F_N2, out of the slope.

title: 0.02 mm caliper reading 41.38 mm
description: A caliper with a 0.02 mm sliding scale holding a ball, reading 41.38 mm, with a close-up strip of its scales
caption: A caliper whose sliding scale has 50 divisions over 49 mm, so it reads to 0.02 mm, holding a ball. The close-up strip shows the sliding scale’s zero just past 41 mm, and its 19th mark, four marks past the 3, lined up with a main-scale mark: 41 + 19 × 0.02 = 41.38 mm.

title: 0.1 mm caliper reading 34.7 mm
description: A caliper with a 0.1 mm sliding scale holding a cylinder, reading 34.7 mm, with a close-up strip of its scales
caption: A caliper whose sliding scale has 10 divisions over 9 mm, so it reads to 0.1 mm, holding an upright cylinder across its diameter. The close-up strip shows the sliding scale’s zero between 34 and 35 mm on the main scale and its 7th mark lined up with a main-scale mark, so the reading is 34.7 mm.

title: Caliper reading 23.45 mm
description: A caliper holding a block, reading 23.45 mm on its 0.05 mm sliding scale, with a close-up strip of its scales
caption: A 150 mm caliper with a block held between its outside jaws. The close-up strip below it shows the sliding scale’s zero just past 23 mm on the main scale, and its 9th mark, between the 4 and the 5, lined up with a main-scale mark: 23 + 9 × 0.05 = 23.45 mm. The least count, 0.05 mm, is printed on the slider.

title: Caliper scales close-up: 62.35 mm
description: A close-up strip of a caliper’s main scale and 0.05 mm sliding scale reading 62.35 mm
caption: The scales alone, without the caliper: the main scale from 6 to 11 cm and the 0.05 mm sliding scale below it, its zero just past 62 mm, and its 7th mark, between the 3 and the 4, lined up with a main-scale mark, so the reading is 62 + 7 × 0.05 = 62.35 mm.

title: Caliper with a zero error
description: Two 0.1 mm calipers: above, with its jaws closed, reading 0.3 mm; below, holding block A, reading 27.6 mm, each with a close-up strip of its scales
caption: The same 0.1 mm caliper twice. Above, with its jaws closed, the sliding scale’s zero sits just past the main scale’s zero and its 3rd mark lines up: a zero error of +0.3 mm. Below, holding block A, it reads 27.6 mm. Students take the zero error off the reading: the block is 27.3 mm long.

title: Metric ruler reading 7.45 cm
description: A 15 cm ruler marked in millimeters with a metal cylinder lying along it from 0 to 7.45 cm, with a magnified view of its right end
caption: A 15 cm ruler marked every millimeter, with a metal cylinder lying along it, its left end on 0. Its right end falls halfway between 7.4 and 7.5 cm, so its length is 7.45 cm, the hundredths digit estimated. A magnified view shows the right end against the marks.

title: Micrometer reading 7.38 mm
description: A micrometer holding a ball bearing, reading 7.38 mm, with a magnified view of its sleeve and thimble
caption: A 0–25 mm micrometer with a ball between its anvil and spindle. The magnifier shows the 7 mm mark showing on the sleeve, but not the 7.5 mm mark below the datum line, and the thimble’s 38th mark on the datum line, so the reading is 7 + 0.38 = 7.38 mm. The thimble’s marks bunch together toward its top and bottom edges, as on a real one.

title: Micrometer reading estimated to 0.001 mm: 6.847 mm
description: A micrometer holding a cylinder, reading 6.847 mm, with a magnified view showing the datum line between the thimble’s 34th and 35th marks
caption: A micrometer read one digit past its marks. The magnifier shows the 6.5 mm mark uncovered below the sleeve’s datum line, and the datum line about 0.7 of the way from the thimble’s 34th mark to its 35th, so the reading is 6.5 + 0.347 = 6.847 mm. The last digit is estimated, so 6.846 or 6.848 mm is as good an answer.

title: Micrometer reading just past half a millimeter: 5.51 mm
description: A micrometer holding a wire, reading 5.51 mm, with a magnified view showing the 5.5 mm mark just uncovered on the sleeve
caption: A micrometer measuring a wire, with the thimble’s edge just past the 5.5 mm mark below the sleeve’s datum line, and the thimble’s 1st mark on the datum line. The reading is 5.5 + 0.01 = 5.51 mm. Missing the half-millimeter mark would give 5.01 mm, the common mistake.

title: Micrometer with a negative zero error
description: Two micrometers: above, closed, its thimble’s 0 three marks above the datum line, reading −0.03 mm; below, holding a wire, reading 3.27 mm, each with a magnified view
caption: The same micrometer twice. Above, closed, the thimble’s 0 has turned three marks past the datum line, so it reads −0.03 mm: a negative zero error. Below, holding a wire, it reads 3.27 mm. Taking off the zero error gives 3.27 − (−0.03) = 3.30 mm.

title: Matching position–time, velocity–time and acceleration–time graphs
description: Position–time, velocity–time and acceleration–time graphs stacked on one time axis for a cart that goes forward, stops, then goes back, each segment in its own line style, with the segment ends lettered A to F
caption: Three graphs of one motion stacked on the same time axis: position, velocity and acceleration. The cart speeds up forward from A to B, moves at 4 m/s from B to C, slows to a stop at D, speeds up backward from D to E and slows to a stop again at F. Each segment has its own line style, and the segment ends are lettered A to F on every graph.

title: Position–time graph shapes without numbers
description: A position–time graph with no numbers or gridlines, lettered A to F: curving upward, straight, curving over, flat, then a straight line sloping down
caption: A position–time graph on plain axes with no numbers or gridlines, so only the shapes show. From A to B the line curves upward (speeding up), from B to C it is straight (constant velocity), from C to D it curves over (slowing down), from D to E it is flat (at rest), and from E to F it slopes straight down (moving back at a constant velocity).

title: Position–time graph: speeding up, constant velocity, slowing down, lettered
description: A position–time graph with its segment ends lettered A to E: curving upward from A to B, a straight line from B to C, curving over and leveling off from C to D, and flat from D to E
caption: A position–time graph of a cart that speeds up from rest for 4 s, moves at a constant 4 m/s for 4 s, slows down to a stop over 4 s and stays at rest for 3 s. Its segment ends are lettered A to E: the line curves upward from A to B, is straight from B to C, curves over from C to D, and is flat from D to E.

title: Tangent to a position–time graph for instantaneous velocity
description: A position–time graph curving upward for 6 s, with a dashed tangent line touching the curve at 4 s
caption: A position–time graph of a cart speeding up steadily from rest for 6 s, so the line curves upward. A dashed tangent line touches the curve at 4 s; its slope is the cart’s instantaneous velocity at that moment.

title: Velocity–time graph of a cart speeding up and slowing down
description: A velocity–time graph of straight lines lettered A to F: flat at zero from A to B, rising gently from B to C, rising more steeply from C to D, level from D to E, and falling back to zero from E to F
caption: A velocity–time graph made of straight lines, lettered A to F. The cart is at rest from A to B, speeds up to 2 m/s from B to C, speeds up more quickly to 6 m/s from C to D, holds 6 m/s from D to E, and slows to a stop from E to F. The steeper the line, the greater the acceleration.

title: Motion map of a cart that speeds up, moves at a constant velocity, slows down and stops
description: A motion map with a dot every second from t = 0 s to 11 s along a number line from 0 to 35 m, the dots spreading out, then evenly spaced, then closing up, and one last dot labeled 12–15 s, each moving dot with a dashed velocity arrow
caption: A cart speeds up from rest for 4 s, moves at a constant 4 m/s for 4 s, slows down to a stop over 4 s and stays at rest for 3 s, drawn as a dot every second along a number line in meters. The dots spread out, are evenly spaced, then close up, and the stop is one dot labeled 12–15 s. Each moving dot has a dashed velocity arrow above it, on one scale, so the arrows grow and shrink with the speed.

title: Motion map at a constant velocity
description: A motion map of seven evenly spaced dots, 3 m apart from 0 to 18 m, labeled t = 0 s to 6 s, each with an equal dashed velocity arrow, and a = 0 written above them
caption: An object moving at a constant 3 m/s for 6 s, as a dot every second along a number line from 0 to 18 m. The dots are evenly spaced, 3 m apart, and every velocity arrow is the same length. Above the dots, a = 0: the velocity doesn’t change.

title: Dots-only motion map: draw the velocity arrows
description: A motion map with dots only, no arrows, lettered A to I along a number line from 0 to 22 m: evenly spaced at first, then spreading out, then closing up to a stop
caption: A motion map with no arrows, for students to draw the velocity arrow at each dot. The object moves at 2 m/s for 3 s, speeds up to 5 m/s over 3 s, then slows to a stop over 2 s, a dot every second, lettered A to I. The answer key lists what it does in each segment.

title: Motion map of an object slowing down to a stop
description: A motion map of dots closing up from left to right, labeled t = 0 s to 4 s, then one dot labeled 5–7 s, with dashed velocity arrows getting shorter, and the total displacement Δx drawn under the number line
caption: An object moving at 6 m/s for 1 s, then slowing down steadily to a stop over 4 s and staying at rest for 2 s, as a dot every second. The gaps shrink by 1.5 m each second and the velocity arrows get shorter, until the dots meet at one spot, labeled 5–7 s, with no arrow. An arrow under the number line shows the total displacement, Δx.

title: Motion map of an object speeding up from rest
description: A motion map of seven dots lettered A to G, the gaps between them growing from left to right, with dashed velocity arrows getting longer and an acceleration arrow labeled a pointing right above them
caption: An object speeding up steadily from rest to 6 m/s over 6 s, as a dot every second, lettered A to G. Each gap is 1 m longer than the one before, and the velocity arrows get longer from dot to dot; the first dot, at rest, has none. The acceleration arrow above the dots points the way it moves.

title: Motion map of a cart going out and back, lettered to match its motion graph
description: A motion map of a cart drawn on two lines: on the lower one it speeds up, moves steadily and slows to a stop at D, lettered A to D at the segment ends; on the line above it speeds up back toward the start and slows to a stop at F, with acceleration arrows above each segment
caption: A cart speeds up forward from A to B, moves at 4 m/s from B to C and slows to a stop at D; then it speeds up backward from D to E and slows to a stop again at F. The way back is drawn above the way there, so no dots overlap. The letters at the segment ends are the same as on the matching Motion Graph example, and an acceleration arrow, or a = 0, sits above each segment.

title: Ball launched horizontally off a cliff
description: A ball launched horizontally off the top of a cliff with velocity v_0, drawn again at four equal time steps along its dashed path, with g down and the cliff’s height h and range R marked
caption: A ball launched horizontally from the top corner of a cliff, with its launch velocity v_0 and the acceleration due to gravity g pointing down. The ball is drawn again at four equal time steps along its dashed path, the last where it lands: evenly spaced across, but farther apart each step down. The cliff’s height h and the range R are marked.

title: Projectile launched at 30° with its velocity components
description: A ball launched from level ground at 30°, with the launch velocity v_0, its components v_0x and v_0y, and the dashed parabolic path to where it lands
caption: A ball launched from level ground at 30° above the horizontal, the angle labeled 30°. The launch velocity v_0 is drawn at the ball, with its horizontal and vertical components v_0x and v_0y, and a dashed parabola shows the path to where the ball lands on the ground.

title: Projectile with its maximum height and range labeled
description: A ball launched at 45° with velocity v_0, its dashed path, g pointing down, the maximum height marked H and the range marked R
caption: A ball launched from level ground at 45°, the angle marked θ, with its launch velocity v_0 and the acceleration due to gravity g pointing down. Its maximum height is marked H and its range along the ground R.

title: Projectile path with the ball at equal time steps, lettered
description: A ball launched at 60° from level ground, shown at the launch and six equal time steps along its path, lettered A to G
caption: A ball launched from level ground at 60°, with its dashed path and the ball drawn at the launch and at six equal time steps after it, lettered A to G from the launch to the landing. No vectors are drawn, so students can add the velocity or acceleration at each point.

title: Sketch the path: ball launched upward off a cliff
description: A ball on the top corner of a cliff with a launch velocity v_0 at θ above the horizontal and the cliff’s height marked h, with no path drawn
caption: A ball on the top corner of a cliff, launched at 30° above the horizontal with velocity v_0, the angle marked θ, and the cliff’s height marked h. The path is left off, so students sketch it themselves.

title: Atwood machine with tension, weight and acceleration
description: An Atwood machine: masses m_1 and m_2 hanging over one fixed pulley, with tension T up each side of the string, weights m_1 g and m_2 g down, and dashed acceleration arrows a, up on the left and down on the right
caption: Two blocks, m_1 on the left and m_2 on the right, hang from one string over a fixed pulley hung from the ceiling. Tension T is drawn on each side of the string, pulling up on each block and down on the pulley, and the weights m_1 g and m_2 g point down from the blocks. Dashed acceleration arrows a point up beside m_1 and down beside m_2.

title: Atwood machine with three masses
description: An Atwood machine with m_1 on the left, m_2 on the right and m_3 hanging below m_2 on a second string, with tensions T_1 and T_2, weights m_1 g, m_2 g and m_3 g, and dashed acceleration arrows a
caption: Blocks m_1 and m_2 hang from one string over a fixed pulley, and a third block, m_3, hangs below m_2 on a second string. Tension T_1 is drawn at both ends of the first string and T_2 at both ends of the second, and the weights m_1 g, m_2 g and m_3 g point straight down. Dashed acceleration arrows a point up beside m_1 and down beside m_2 and m_3.

title: Block and tackle with 3 strands holding up the load
description: A block and tackle: a load m hanging from a bar under a movable pulley, held up by three strands of rope, with tension T up each strand, T down at the free end, and the weight mg
caption: A block and tackle with a load m held up by three strands of one rope, running over two fixed pulleys at the ceiling and a movable pulley on a bar above the load. Tension T points up in each of the three strands holding the load and down at the free end, where the effort pulls, and the load’s weight mg points down.

title: Block on an incline tied over a pulley to a hanging mass
description: A block m_1 on a ramp at angle θ, tied by a string over a pulley at the top of the ramp to a hanging block m_2, with tension, weights and the normal force drawn
caption: A block m_1 on a smooth ramp at 40°, its angle marked θ, tied by a string running parallel to the slope over a pulley at the top of the ramp to a block m_2 hanging beside the ramp’s tall side. Tension T is drawn along the string, the weights m_1 g and m_2 g point straight down and the normal force F_N points out of the slope.

title: Block on a table pulled by a hanging mass over a pulley
description: A block m_1 on a rough table tied over a pulley at the table’s edge to a hanging block m_2, with tension, weight, normal force, friction and acceleration arrows
caption: A block m_1 on a rough, hatched table is tied by a string over a pulley at the table’s edge to a block m_2 hanging below. Tension T runs along both parts of the string; m_1 g and m_2 g point down, the normal force F_N points up from m_1, and friction F_f points away from the pulley. Dashed arrows a show m_1 moving toward the pulley and m_2 falling.

title: Cart on a table and a hanging mass, masses left blank
description: A cart on a smooth table tied over a pulley to a hanging block, with blank lines on the cart and the block for their masses
caption: A cart on a smooth table, tied by a string over a pulley at the table’s edge to a block hanging below. Both have a blank line in place of a label, so you can write in the masses for your problem. No forces are drawn.

title: Blank converging lens ray diagram worksheet
description: A blank ray diagram of a converging lens with F, F′, 2F and 2F′ marked on the principal axis, an object between F and 2F, and a numbered cm scale underneath, with no rays drawn
caption: A converging lens of focal length 10 cm on its principal axis with F, F′, 2F and 2F′ marked and an object 15 cm away, between F and 2F, and no rays: a template for students to draw the principal rays and find the image. A cm scale numbered from the lens runs under it, for measuring the image distance.

title: Concave mirror ray diagram: object between C and F
description: A ray diagram of a concave mirror with F and C marked, an object between C and F, four principal rays, and a real, inverted, larger image beyond C
caption: A concave mirror of focal length 10 cm with an object 15 cm away, between C and F. Four rays reflect from it: parallel then through F, through F then parallel, through C and back on itself, and off the vertex at the same angle. They meet 30 cm in front of the mirror, beyond C, at the real, inverted image twice the object’s size.

title: Converging lens with the object at 2F
description: A ray diagram of a converging lens with the object at 2F and a real, inverted image of the same size at 2F′, with the object and image distances marked d_o and d_i
caption: A converging lens of focal length 10 cm with the object at 2F, 20 cm away. The three principal rays meet at 2F′ on the far side, where the image is real, inverted and the same size as the object. Arrows below the axis mark the object distance d_o and the image distance d_i.

title: Converging lens ray diagram: object beyond 2F
description: A ray diagram of a converging lens with F, F′, 2F and 2F′ marked, an object O beyond 2F, three principal rays, and a real, inverted, smaller image I between F′ and 2F′
caption: A converging lens of focal length 10 cm with an object 4 cm tall, 30 cm away, beyond 2F. Three principal rays leave the object’s tip: parallel then through F′, straight through the center, and through F then parallel. They meet between F′ and 2F′, where the real, inverted, smaller image is drawn.

title: Convex mirror ray diagram
description: A ray diagram of a convex mirror with F and C behind it; the reflected rays spread out and their dashed extensions meet behind the mirror at a small, upright, virtual image
caption: A convex mirror of focal length 10 cm, its F and C behind it, with an object 20 cm in front. Each ray reflects outward: the parallel one as if from F, the one heading for F back parallel, the one heading for C back on itself, and the one at the vertex at the same angle. Dashed extensions meet behind the mirror at the virtual, upright, smaller image.

title: Diverging lens ray diagram
description: A ray diagram of a diverging lens with an object beyond 2F; the rays spread out and their dashed extensions meet between the lens and F at a small, upright, virtual image
caption: A diverging lens of focal length 10 cm with an object 20 cm away. The parallel ray spreads out as if from F, the ray heading for F′ leaves parallel, and the center ray goes straight on. Their dashed extensions meet between F and the lens, at the virtual, upright, smaller image, drawn dashed.

title: Magnifying glass ray diagram: object inside F
description: A ray diagram of a converging lens with the object inside F; the rays spread out after the lens and their dashed extensions meet behind the object at a dashed, upright, larger virtual image
caption: A converging lens of focal length 10 cm used as a magnifying glass, with a 3 cm object 5 cm away, inside F. The rays spread apart after the lens, so they never meet; their dashed extensions meet on the object’s side, 10 cm from the lens, at the virtual, upright image twice the object’s size, drawn dashed.

title: Plane mirror ray diagram
description: A ray diagram of a plane mirror with an object 15 cm in front; two rays from its tip reflect at equal angles and their dashed extensions meet behind the mirror at an upright virtual image the same size, 15 cm behind
caption: A plane mirror with an object 4 cm tall, 15 cm in front of it. Two rays from the object’s tip reflect at equal angles, one off the mirror level with the object’s foot and one above the tip. Their dashed extensions meet behind the mirror at the virtual image, upright and the same size, 15 cm behind it, the distances marked d_o and d_i.

title: 5 N spring scale with slotted masses
description: A green 5 N spring scale holding a hanger with four slotted masses, the pointer at 2.45 N, with a magnified view
caption: A green 5 N spring scale, numbered every 0.5 N and marked every 0.1 N, holding a hanger with four slotted masses stacked on it. The pointer sits between the 2.4 and 2.5 N marks, shown enlarged in the magnifier beside the scale.

title: 50 N spring scale in newtons and grams
description: A black and white 50 N spring scale printed in newtons on the left and grams on the right, with a block on its hook and the pointer at 27.50 N (2750 g)
caption: A 50 N spring scale drawn in black and white, printed in newtons left of the slot and grams right of it: 0 to 50 N, numbered every 5 N and marked every 0.5 N, and 0 to 5000 g. A block hangs from its hook and the pointer sits on the 27.5 N mark, level with 2750 g, shown in the magnifier beside it.

title: Spring scale reading 6.25 N
description: A tan 10 N spring scale with a block on its hook, the pointer at 6.25 N, with a magnified view of the pointer
caption: A tan 10 N spring scale, numbered every 1 N and marked every 0.1 N, with a block hanging from its hook. The pointer is between the 6.2 and 6.3 N marks, and a magnified circle beside the scale shows the marks around it.

title: Spring scale reading in grams
description: A pink 1 N spring scale printed in grams, from 0 to 100 g, with a block on its hook and the pointer at 45.5 g
caption: A pink 1 N spring scale printed only in grams, its tag reading 100 g, from 0 to 100 g, numbered every 10 g and marked every 1 g, with a block on its hook. The pointer is between the 45 and 46 g marks, shown in the magnifier beside it.

title: Spring scale with a zero error
description: Two 10 N spring scales: on the left, with nothing hanging, the pointer rests at 0.20 N; on the right, with a block, it reads 4.30 N
caption: The same 10 N spring scale twice. On the left, with nothing on its hook, the pointer rests below zero, at 0.20 N; on the right, with a block hanging, it points to 4.30 N. Students take the zero error off the reading to find the force.

title: Adding three vectors head to tail
description: On a grid, vectors A, B and C drawn head to tail, A to the right, B up and to the right, C up and to the left, with the dashed resultant R from A’s tail to C’s tip
caption: Three vectors drawn to scale head to tail on a grid: A, 5 squares to the right; B, 4 squares at 60°; and C, 3 squares at 150°, up and to the left. The dashed resultant R runs from the first tail to the last tip.

title: Adding two perpendicular vectors head to tail
description: On a grid, vector A 6 squares to the right, then vector B 8 squares up from its tip, with the dashed resultant R from A’s tail to B’s tip and its angle marked θ
caption: Two vectors drawn to scale head to tail on a grid: A, 6 squares to the right, then B, 8 squares straight up from A’s tip. The dashed resultant R runs from A’s tail to B’s tip, with its angle above the horizontal marked θ.

title: Resolving a vector into x and y components
description: On a grid with x and y axes, vector A at θ above the x axis, with its dashed components A_x along the x axis and A_y up to A’s tip
caption: One vector A, 5 squares long at 37° above the horizontal, drawn from where the x and y axes cross, on a grid. Its angle is marked θ from the x axis, and its components A_x along the horizontal and A_y up to its tip are drawn as thinner dashed arrows.

title: Subtracting vectors: A − B as A + (−B)
description: On a grid, vector A 5 squares to the right, then −B 3 squares straight down from its tip, with the dashed resultant A − B
caption: Vector subtraction drawn as addition: A, 5 squares to the right, then −B, 3 squares straight down from A’s tip, the opposite of a B pointing up. The dashed resultant from A’s tail to −B’s tip is labeled A − B.

title: Vector addition worksheet: draw the resultant
description: On a grid, vector A 4 squares at 30° and vector B 5 squares at 120° drawn head to tail, with no resultant drawn
caption: Two vectors drawn to scale head to tail on a grid: A, 4 squares at 30°, and B, 5 squares at 120°, starting from A’s tip. The resultant is left off, so students draw it from A’s tail to B’s tip and measure it.

title: Displacement–time graph of a wave: period and frequency
description: A transverse wave on axes of displacement in cm against time in s, four cycles over 2 seconds, with tick marks instead of gridlines and its period T marked from crest to crest
caption: A wave drawn against time instead of distance: four cycles over 2 seconds, on numbered axes with tick marks rather than gridlines. The period T is marked from one crest to the next and the amplitude is left for students, who work out the frequency from the period.

title: Label the compression and rarefaction of a longitudinal wave
description: A longitudinal wave of vertical lines over a distance axis in m, with its wavelength λ marked from one compression to the next and blank lines under a compression and a rarefaction
caption: A longitudinal wave, like a sound wave, drawn as vertical lines over a numbered distance axis. Its wavelength λ is marked from the middle of one compression to the next. Blank lines under a compression and a rarefaction are for students to name them.

title: Label the parts of a wave worksheet
description: A transverse wave about a dashed rest line, with no axes, with blank lines for its wavelength, amplitude, a crest and a trough
caption: A transverse wave two and a half cycles long, drawn about a dashed rest line with no axes. Arrows mark its wavelength and amplitude, and a crest and a trough are pointed out, each with a blank line for students to write what it is.

title: Longitudinal wave above its matching transverse wave
description: A longitudinal wave drawn as vertical lines, bunched at a compression and spread at a rarefaction, above a transverse wave on a displacement–distance grid, the compressions directly over the crests
caption: A longitudinal wave drawn as a row of vertical lines, above the transverse wave it matches on numbered axes. The lines bunch together at each compression, right above a crest, and spread apart at each rarefaction, above a trough. A compression, a rarefaction, a crest and a trough are labeled, and the wavelength λ and amplitude A are marked.

title: Measure the wavelength and amplitude of a wave
description: A transverse wave three cycles long on a grid of displacement in cm against distance in m, numbered every meter and centimeter, with nothing marked
caption: A transverse wave three cycles long on numbered axes with gridlines, displacement in centimeters against distance in meters. Nothing is marked, so students read the wavelength and the amplitude off the axes.

title: Transverse wave with its wavelength and amplitude labeled
description: A transverse wave on a grid of displacement in cm against distance in m, two and a half cycles long, with its wavelength λ marked from crest to crest, its amplitude A from the rest line up to a crest, and a crest and a trough labeled
caption: A transverse wave two and a half cycles long on numbered axes, displacement in centimeters against distance in meters, with gridlines. Its wavelength λ is marked with an arrow from one crest to the next, its amplitude A from the rest line up to the first crest, and a crest and a trough are labeled.
